items.title: [FEATURE] groupletChoice with multiple selection
items.body:
### Summary

`groupletChoice` sets one value. Add a `multiple=True` variant where each click adds or removes the tile's value from a comma separated list, every chosen tile showing the selected state.

### Problem or Need

A step that picks several options out of N has no tile equivalent: it falls back to `checkBoxText`, which breaks the visual language of the choice step around it. Real case: the service classes of a structure (`anc_cnv.se_fornitore.classi_servizio`) in anaci's "Nuovo servizio" wizard, a `checkBoxText` today.

### Proposed Solution

- `multiple=False` kwarg on `gr_groupletChoice`. With `True` the click calls a new `gnr_grouplet.choiceToggle`, which toggles the tile's value in `field` and rebuilds the string by walking the tiles: the same set always writes the same value, whatever the click order, as `checkBoxText` does with its checkboxes. Nothing selected writes `null`.
- `caption_field` collects the captions of the selected tiles instead of the single one.
- The selected-state controller tests membership in the list instead of equality.
- A `grouplet_choice_multiple` class keeps the tick always visible, grey until the tile is picked, so the tiles read as checkboxes and not as an exclusive choice.
- `autoNext` does not apply to a multiple choice and is ignored.

### Considered Alternatives

Keeping `checkBoxText`: it already stores this format, but it cannot look like the tiles next to it. Toggling in click order instead of tile order: fewer lines, but the same set would then write different strings.

### Impact and Scope

`resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.py`, `grouplet.js` and `grouplet.css`, plus the test page `test/webpages/gnrwdg/test_grouplets/14_grouplet_choice.py`. Default behaviour unchanged. Same limit as `checkBoxText`: a value containing a comma cannot be represented.

items.title: docs(grouplet): For Dummies tour of the grouplet family
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a multi-tab self-contained HTML documentation site that walks through the 7 widgets in the grouplet family — `grouplet`, `groupletChunk`, `groupletForm`, `groupletPanel`, `groupletWizard`, `groupletGrid`, Topic Grid — plus the three `genro.dlg.*DataEditor` variants and a final cheat sheet.

## Layout

```
docs/grouplet-family-for-dummies/
├── index.html       # shell: dark theme, tab navigation, copy buttons
├── serve.py         # zero-dep launcher (stdlib http.server)
└── tabs/
    ├── why.html         # overview + reactive flow SVG
    ├── quickstart.html  # minimal handler + minimal resource
    ├── grouplet.html    # the base widget
    ├── chunk.html       # groupletChunk + template syntax
    ├── form.html        # groupletForm + memory/record stores
    ├── panel.html       # tree / multiButton navigation
    ├── wizard.html      # step-by-step (with stepper SVG)
    ├── grid.html        # groupletGrid (architecture SVG + 7 modes)
    ├── topic.html       # CSS grid of folder of grouplets
    ├── dialogs.html     # memory/document/recordDataEditor
    └── cheatsheet.html  # 43-row "I want to..." reference + anti-patterns
```

Total: 13 files, ~2385 added lines.

## How to view

```bash
python3 docs/grouplet-family-for-dummies/serve.py
# opens http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in the browser
```

Direct `file://` doesn't work because `index.html` uses `fetch()` to load the tab fragments, which the browser blocks for CORS on local files. The launcher script picks a free port automatically (8000+), serves the directory, and opens the browser.

Flags: `--port N` for explicit port, `--no-browser` to skip auto-open.

## Why fragments instead of one monolithic HTML

Multi-file is friendlier for refactoring — each tab can be edited independently without touching the shell, and the shell's CSS/JS is shared (no duplication). Tradeoff is that `file://` doesn't work; `serve.py` is the answer.

## Tone and content

Each tab follows a consistent shape:

1. One-sentence elevator pitch
2. "When to use" / "Why" (problem framing, not API listing)
3. Quick example, code is copy-pasteable
4. One or more advanced patterns
5. Full parameters table
6. Gotchas (as warning call-outs)
7. Reference files (source paths under `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/` and the test webpages)

Code samples are grounded on the actual test files under `projects/gnrcore/packages/test/webpages/gnrwdg/test_grouplets/` (legacy family) and `test_grouplet_grid/` (new from #905). The reader is assumed to know GenroPy basics (Bag, datapath, formbuilder) — no remedial explanations.

## Related issues

Several silent-failure modes surfaced during the read-through and are filed in companion issues:

- #909 — umbrella bug: silent collisions on `name=` / `formId=` / `frameCode=` registries, missing `@public_method` not raising, `handler+resource` precedence undefined, etc.
- #910 — RFC discussion: should `grouplet` accept a client-side `handlerJs=` for static templates that don't need a server round-trip? Includes a measurement plan and three decisional alternatives.

## Test plan

Documentation-only PR — no production code changes.

- [x] All 11 tab fragments parse as valid HTML (no `<html>`/`<head>`/`<body>` wrappers, no `<style>`/`<script>` blocks)
- [x] All fragments served via `python -m http.server` return HTTP 200 (smoke-tested locally)
- [x] No AI/LLM references in any of the 13 files (greps clean)
- [x] `flake8` clean on `serve.py` (zero errors, strict mode)
- [x] `python3 -m py_compile serve.py` passes
- [x] Server launcher tested with auto-port detection and `--port`/`--no-browser` flags
- [ ] Reviewer to verify the doc renders correctly on Chrome / Firefox / Safari

## Suggested follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Hook the doc into a wider GenroPy docs index when one exists
- Consider auto-publishing to GitHub Pages on tag releases
- Iterate on tab content as the family evolves (e.g. when #910 lands, add a "JS handler" subsection to the relevant tabs)

items.title: [TASK] Redesign the dynamic field form and fix its bugs

labels.name: task
labels.description: Technical task, maintenance, or internal improvement

items.body:
### Summary

Redesign the dynamic field form (`df_fieldsBagForm` / `df_customTabs` in `gnrcomponents/dynamicform`) and fix its bugs.

### Objective

The form that defines a dynamic field is hard to use. Widget attributes are stored in two places for no clear reason: some go in `wdg_kwargs`, others at the top level of the record. Anything without a dedicated field can only be set through **Extended Parameters**, a key/value editor over the whole record. Nothing in that editor says that a key becomes a widget attribute.

Example: giving a `dbSelect` a `condition` (e.g. `$visibile_sede_corrente IS TRUE`) is only possible by adding a `condition` key there.

Goal: every supported attribute gets its own field, stored in one place, and the labels say what each field does.

### Scope

Bugs:
- Data getter tab: two fields are labelled "Column"; the second one is actually `innerpath`.
- Format defaults set by `onDataTypeChange` (`short`, `Yes,No`, …) are written to `record.format`, but `df_makeDynamicField` always overwrites `format` with `field_format`, so the defaults never apply.
- "Vocal input" is shown for every widget, but only `simpleTextArea` reads it. On a text area `speech` defaults to True, so voice input is on even while the checkbox shows unchecked.
- The "Graph" data type can be selected, but it renders "Not yet implemented".
- `documentation`, `querable` and `calculated` are not popped and end up as stray attributes on the widget.
- Labels without `!!` are never localized: Page, Dflt.Value, Hidden Group, Table, Where, Column.

Redesign:
- Give `dbSelect`/`dbCombobox` dedicated fields: Source picked from a list of tables (now free text `pkg.table`), plus Condition, Columns/auxColumns and Order by.
- Store each widget attribute in a single place (`wdg_kwargs` or the top level, not both). Existing records need migrating.
- Keep Extended Parameters only for advanced or debug use, not as the normal way to set attributes.
- Group the tabs by purpose: data, validation, visibility, appearance. Move Page out of the first row.
- Clarify labels: Range vs Std.Range (the first rejects the value, the second only shows a warning), Help (it is the tooltip), Visible if (needs a JS expression on field codes: add a ghost/example), Hidden Group, Keepable value, Querable → Queryable.
- Hide Graph until it is implemented.

### Technical Details / Notes

To check before removing: whether Data getter and Hidden Group are actually used in projects.

items.title: [FEATURE] groupletWizard: terminal state as a resource, initial step, and no reposition on a self-triggered reload
items.body:
## Summary

`groupletWizard` works beautifully as a "fill everything, then commit" flow. Using
it as the editor of a **document** — something that is saved, reopened, and later
frozen — runs into three limits that all sit in the same place: what the wizard
does when the form loads, and what its terminal page is allowed to be.

## Problem or Need

Building a delivery-note wizard (type picker, header, rows, recap) on top of
`groupletWizard`, against `packages/test/resources/tables/booking` as the
reference.

**1. The terminal page can only be a template.** `summary_template` on the
topic's `__info__` gives the wizard a summary page rendered as
`div(template=summary_template, datasource=value)`
(`gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.py`, `gr_groupletWizard`). A client-side
template can substitute `$field` and drop empty blocks, and that is all: it has
no join, so FK columns print their stored code instead of the related caption; it
cannot repeat a collection, so the document's rows cannot be listed; and it
cannot carry a widget, so the page that logically owns "confirm" / "print" /
"reopen" has nowhere to put them.

Every wizard STEP, by contrast, is rendered by an RPC (`gr_loadGrouplet`) and can
do all three — query, loop, emit widgets. The terminal page is the one surface
that cannot.

**2. A saved record cannot be opened on a chosen step.** Without a summary, the
`formsubscribe_onLoaded` controller runs `wizardGoTo(this, 0, frameCode)`, so a
record that already exists opens on step 1 — for a wizard whose step 1 is a
document-type picker, an already-issued document greets the user with the type
picker. With a summary it opens on the summary instead, which is the right idea
but lands on the limited page of point 1. There is no parameter for the step a
wizard starts on.

**3. The wizard repositions itself on the reload of its own save.** The same
`formsubscribe_onLoaded` controller fires on EVERY form load, including the
reload that necessarily follows the insert of a new record (the pkey and any
counter-assigned field come back from the server). Sequence, measured live:

- `wizardNext` saves the step form into the main record, publishes
  `<frameCode>_step_complete`, then bumps `step_index`;
- the main record is now dirty, so the form saves and inserts;
- the insert reloads the form, `onLoaded` fires, and the wizard repositions — to
  step 0 with no summary, to the summary page with one.

The reload resolves one frame after the advance, so the step the user has just
reached is abandoned. In practice this means the wizard cannot be combined with a
form that saves while the steps are running (a store `autoSave`, or an explicit
save subscribed to `_step_complete`) — which is exactly what a document that must
exist as a draft from the first advance needs. `booking` never hits this because
it never saves in the middle: `th_booking.py` carries dialog sizes and
`showtoolbar=False`, nothing else, and `saveMainFormOnComplete` inserts once at
the end.

## Proposed Solution

1. **`summary_resource`** on the topic's `__info__`, as an alternative to
   `summary_template`: a grouplet resource rendered like any step (same remote,
   same `grouplet_remote_*` values), so the terminal page can resolve captions,
   list rows and carry buttons. `summary_template` stays for the simple case.

2. **`startStep`** on `gr_groupletWizard` — an index, or a grouplet code —
   deciding where the wizard opens. A useful default would be: a new record on
   the first step, a saved one on the terminal page (which is already the
   behaviour when a summary exists, but it should not depend on the summary).

3. **Do not reposition on a self-triggered reload.** The onLoaded controller
   should reposition when the form loads a DIFFERENT record, not when it reloads
   the one already being edited — a guard on the loaded pkey, or an explicit
   opt-out. That alone makes a save-as-you-go wizard possible.

## Considered Alternatives

- Rendering the terminal page as a wizard STEP: works, and it is what we do now,
  but then a saved record opens on step 1 (point 2), and the stepper invites the
  user back into steps that no longer apply once the document is issued.
- Keeping the record unsaved until the last step (booking's shape): this is what
  we settled on, and it is fine — but it rules out any flow where the document
  must exist while it is being written, and point 3 is what forces the choice
  rather than a design decision.
- A `dataController` declared after the wizard, subscribed to the same
  `formsubscribe_onLoaded` and setting `.step_index` afterwards: it would run
  second and might work, but it is racing framework behaviour rather than using
  it.

## Impact and Scope

Anyone using `groupletWizard` for a document rather than a one-shot form:
anything with a draft state, a protocol/number assigned on confirm, or a
terminal page that has to show related data and actions. Points 1 and 2 are
additive; point 3 changes behaviour for a case that today cannot work at all,
since a wizard whose form saves mid-flow loses the user's position.

## Additional Information

Verified on `develop`, August 2026, against
`resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.py` (`gr_groupletWizard`,
`_getGroupletsRootInfo`), `gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.js` (`wizardNext`,
`wizardGoTo`) and `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_frm.js` (`doAutoSave`).

Related, and worth a line in the docs whatever is decided: in a th form the
wizard must be mounted as `form.center.contentPane().groupletWizard(...)` with a
RELATIVE `value='^.record'`. `groupletWizard` returns a framePane, which needs a
parent that is already sized, and the step form is a memory store whose
`store_locationpath` is that value resolved through `absDatapath` — an absolute
`'^#FORM.record'` leaves it at `status='noItem'` with every field disabled.

items.title: Support _packages pattern for grouplet resource override
items.body:
## Problem

The `_packages/<pkg_name>/` pattern for resource customization is currently supported only for table resources (in `gnrresourceloader.py:552`). Grouplet resources loaded via `mixinComponent(f'{grouplets_root}/{resource}')` do not support this pattern.

This means that if package A defines `resources/grouplets/my_grouplet.py`, package B cannot override it via `resources/grouplets/_packages/A/my_grouplet.py`. The only option is to create `resources/grouplets/my_grouplet.py` directly in package B, which overwrites the grouplet for ALL packages, not just for package A's context.

## Use case

Package `helpdesk` (from gnrsupport) defines a generic `operator_assistance` grouplet. Package `anc_app` (ANACI) needs to customize it by adding application-specific fields (e.g., sede selector). With `_packages` support, anc_app could define:

```
anc_app/resources/grouplets/_packages/helpdesk/operator_assistance.py
```

This would override the grouplet only when loaded from the helpdesk package context, without affecting other packages that might use the same grouplet name.

## Proposed solution

In the grouplet loading code (`gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.py`), after looking for the resource in the standard path, also check for `_packages/<source_pkg>/` overrides, similar to how `loadTableScript` works in `gnrresourceloader.py:549-552`.

## Current workaround

Create `resources/grouplets/operator_assistance.py` directly in the overriding package. This works but is a global override rather than a targeted one.

items.title: RFC: should grouplet accept a client-side handler (handlerJs=)?
items.body:
## Background

Every grouplet today resolves its content through `gr_loadGrouplet` server-side:

- `handler=` is a Python `@public_method` that builds a `GnrDomSrc` tree
- `resource=` is a Python file under `resources/grouplets/` whose `grouplet_main(pane, **kwargs)` builds the same tree
- In both cases the server serializes the resulting struct to XML, the client receives it and mounts the dijits

For `groupletGrid` this is fine: one RPC at boot, then zero RPC because the template lives in client memory as a `GnrDomSource` that the controller deep-clones per row.

For the rest of the family, *every* mount is a server round-trip — even when the grouplet contents are completely static and could equally well be expressed client-side.

## The observation

The fluent builder API used by the Python side (`pane.contentPane(...)._formbuilder(cols=2)._textbox(value='^.x')`) **already has a JS twin** in `gnr.GnrDomSource._()`:

```js
sourceNode._('contentPane', {datapath: '.myform'})
          ._('formbuilder', {cols: 2})
          ._('textbox', {value: '^.email', lbl: 'Email'});
```

defined at [gnrjs/gnr_d20/js/gnrdomsource.js:2050](gnrjs/gnr_d20/js/gnrdomsource.js#L2050). Every existing widget uses it internally (`sourceNode._('div', ...)`, `sourceNode._('button', kw)`, ...). So the machinery to build a struct on the client without a Python round-trip is already there.

## The proposal (to discuss, not necessarily to ship)

Add a third resolution path on `pane.grouplet(...)`:

```python
pane.grouplet(
    value='^.contact',
    handlerJs=\"\"\"
        const fb = pane._('formbuilder', {cols: 2});
        fb._('textbox', {value: '^.email', lbl: 'Email'});
        fb._('textbox', {value: '^.phone', lbl: 'Phone'});
    \"\"\")
```

The string is `funcCreate`-d on the client into a function `(pane, kw) => { ... }` and invoked at mount time, **skipping the `kw.remote = 'gr_loadGrouplet'` round-trip**. The widget would be re-built from scratch every time the value path changes — same as the server-side equivalent — only the resolution lives client-side.

The implementation surface is small: a branch in `gnr.widgets.Grouplet.createContent` at [gnrjs/gnr_d20/js/genro_components.js:3120](gnrjs/gnr_d20/js/genro_components.js#L3120) that, when `handlerJs` is set, replaces the `remote` machinery with a direct `funcCreate(handlerJs, 'pane,kw')(sourceNode._('contentPane', ...), kw)` call. ~20 lines.

## What's gained

- **Zero RPC** at first mount for static grouplets (settings sections, dashboard cards, kanban tile inner template, anything that doesn't query the DB to decide its shape)
- **Symmetry with `groupletGrid`** — the row template is already a client-side struct after the boot RPC; `handlerJs` lets you skip the boot RPC entirely when the template is static
- **Faster initial paint** on pages with many grouplets (settings page with N collapsed sections, dialog editors that all share a template family)
- **Test-friendly** — a client-only grouplet is easier to demo in a fixture / mock environment with no backend

## What's lost / risks

- **No server context** during build: cannot read `self.db`, `self.application.preferences`, table metadata, current user permissions. Anything that needs server-side info has to stay Python.
- **JS source check-in** — the string in the Python side becomes a chunk of JS-as-string, which is awkward to maintain, lint, and test. A heredoc with proper IDE support exists in genropy (the same pattern as `dataController(\"\"\"...js...\"\"\")`) but it has the same pain points.
- **Two parallel handler types** to know about — discovery cost for new contributors. The For Dummies tour just added enough complexity to the family already; adding a third resolution mode is non-trivial cognitive load.
- **No `safe_mode` mixin** — Python resource handlers benefit from `mixinTableResource(table, ..., safeMode=True)` to inject table-specific behaviors. A JS handler has no equivalent.
- **Validation / virtual_columns metadata** — `__info__()` is a Python construct; auto-discovery of template / virtual_columns from a JS handler would need a different mechanism.

## Open questions

1. **Is the latency saving real on production pages?** A typical settings page does 5-10 grouplet RPCs at boot. Each is ~50-150ms. The cumulative gain is 300ms-1.5s. Worth measuring before committing to the API surface.
2. **Should `handlerJs=` cover the `resource=` case too?** I.e., a JS resource file under `resources/grouplets/<name>.js`? This would push the proposal from \"escape hatch\" to \"full second pillar of the framework\" — much bigger commitment.
3. **Is `groupletGrid`'s pattern already the answer?** A `groupletGrid` with a static `resource=` already pays exactly one RPC at boot for the template, then zero. If the use case is \"many copies of the same grouplet on a page\", `groupletGrid` is the right tool — not a new `handlerJs=`. So when *is* the new feature the right answer?
4. **Does `dataController` already cover the lightweight case?** A static `pane.div(...)._('formbuilder', ...)` built inside a `dataController(\"\"\"...js...\"\"\")` produces basically the same effect for tiny inline templates. So is `handlerJs=` really filling a gap, or just packaging an existing pattern?

## Decision needed

Three viable answers:

- **(a) Don't ship.** `groupletGrid` covers the repeated-template case, server-side handlers are cheap enough for the rest, and adding a third resolution mode increases the family's surface area more than the savings justify.
- **(b) Ship as escape hatch.** Land `handlerJs=` on `grouplet` only (not on `groupletForm`/`Panel`/`Wizard`), document it as \"for static templates where you want to skip the boot RPC\", and let usage emerge organically.
- **(c) Investigate first.** Measure boot-time RPC cost on a real settings page (5-10 grouplets). If the saving is < 200ms total, drop the proposal. If it's > 500ms, ship (b).

## Where this came from

While drafting the For Dummies tour of the grouplet family I noted that every grouplet pays an RPC even when the template is provably static. A reader asked \"could a grouplet be JS-only?\" — to which the honest answer is \"no, by design, but technically yes with ~20 lines of code\". This RFC is the writeup of that conversation.

items.title: Grouplet family: surface silent failures and identifier collisions
items.body:
While drafting a "For Dummies" tour of the grouplet family (an internal doc exercise across the 7 widgets — `grouplet`, `groupletChunk`, `groupletForm`, `groupletPanel`, `groupletWizard`, `groupletGrid`, Topic Grid + the three `genro.dlg.*DataEditor` variants), several **silent failure modes** kept surfacing while reading the source side by side with the existing tests. None of them produce a traceback, a log line, or a visible error in the browser — they just produce surprising behavior that costs the developer 15-30 minutes of head-scratching to diagnose.

Filing them as a single umbrella because the fix shape is the same: convert "silent surprise" into "loud signal". Each item below is independent and could be split into its own PR.

## A) Handler missing `@public_method` decorator

When `pane.grouplet(handler=self.my_method)` resolves a handler that isn't decorated with `@public_method`, the RPC roundtrip returns nothing. The pane stays empty, browser shows no error, server log shows nothing.

**Fix shape**: server-side, on `gr_loadGrouplet`, check `getattr(handler, 'is_rpc', False)` and `raise` a `GnrException` like `"grouplet handler '<name>' is not decorated with @public_method"` if not.

## B) `handler=` and `resource=` both passed — `resource` wins silently

`pane.grouplet(value='^.x', handler=self.x_handler, resource='x_template')` silently drops the handler. Today's behavior is to prefer `resource`, with no warning.

**Fix shape**: in the builder, raise `GnrException` if both are non-`None`. (Or accept both and warn loudly; the strict variant is safer.)

## C) Duplicate `name=` across `groupletChunk` / dialog editors

Two chunks with `name='edit'` collide on the page-wide `genro.dlg.memoryDataEditor` registry. The second click reuses the first dialog's `handler` and `title`, inheriting the wrong state. No error.

**Fix shape**: in `genro.dlg._groupletForm` (in `gnrjs/gnr_d20/js/genro_dlg.js`), detect a duplicate `dlgId` already in the registry and either (a) error explicitly, or (b) `console.error` with the conflicting names so the bug is visible in devtools.

## D) Duplicate `formId=` across `groupletForm`

Same shape as C, on a different registry: `genro.formById('gf_main')` returns the first registration; subsequent `groupletForm` instances with the same id silently shadow it and lose all external `load()` / `save()` traffic.

**Fix shape**: at form registration time, warn or error on collision.

## E) Duplicate `frameCode=` across `groupletPanel`

Same shape as D on a third registry: status events cross-fire between panels.

**Fix shape**: same as D.

## F) Grouplet file starting with `__` is silently skipped

The topic menu builder filters children whose name starts with `__` (to hide `__info__.py`, `__pycache__`, etc.). A user-created `__my_section.py` therefore silently disappears from the topic grid.

**Fix shape**: low priority, but a doc string on the filter helps the next reader; alternatively, restrict the filter to a literal denylist (`{'__info__.py', '__pycache__'}`) rather than a prefix match.

## G) `__info__.priority` default of `0` collides with caption-sorted siblings

When some children declare `priority` and others don't, the unset ones default to `0` and sort by caption ahead of `priority=5` children. The author expects "priority controls order"; the system says "priority controls order **only among children that set it**".

**Fix shape**: change the default for unset priority to a high sentinel (`+inf` or `999999`), so unset-priority children sort **after** explicit-priority ones. Alternatively, document the current default loudly in the `__info__()` pattern.

## H) `groupletWizard.wizardGoTo` saves without validation

`wizardNext` calls `form.isValid()` and refuses to advance on errors. But `wizardGoTo` — the action wired on each numbered circle in the stepper bar — saves the current form unconditionally before jumping. If the user clicks backwards in the stepper, an invalid current step is silently saved on its way out.

**Fix shape**: route `wizardGoTo` through the same `isValid()` gate, or add a kwarg `validateOnGoTo=True` (default true) for opt-out.

## I) `groupletChunk` `grid_columns` vs `remote_grid_columns` precedence

When `resource` is a topic, `grid_columns=N` is rewritten internally to `grouplet_remote_grid_columns=N` and merged with any explicit `remote_grid_columns=M`. The precedence is currently undefined (last wins, depending on dict iteration order).

**Fix shape**: define precedence explicitly in `gr_groupletChunk` — either error on both being set, or document a clear winner (the more specific `remote_grid_columns=` wins, and `grid_columns=` is a deprecated shorthand).

---

## How these were found

All nine items were extracted from warning callouts collected while writing a multi-tab "For Dummies" HTML doc across the grouplet family. The exercise — reading the source of each widget side by side with its test files — surfaced these silent failure modes one at a time. They are the actionable distillate of that read-through.

## Suggested cut (one PR per group, smallest first)

1. **C / D / E** — collision warnings; same code shape, same registry-collision pattern, smallest fix.
2. **A / B** — handler/resource explicit errors; biggest "found bug" per unit of fix.
3. **H** — wizardGoTo validation; single-method change.
4. **F / G / I** — these are arguably documentation issues with a loud-warning escalation; convert to whatever feels natural.

Happy to split this into separate issues if preferred.

items.title: feat(doc): one documentation address for grouplets, fields and handbook pages
items.body:
## What

A single documentation endpoint, `sys/ep_doc`, and a single client popup for the docs of grouplet cards, field helpers and handbook pages.

**Address**: `<kind>:<target>:<name>`
| kind | address | source |
|---|---|---|
| `grouplet` | `grouplet:<pkg.table\|pkg>:<resource>` | the card `doc` of the resource (inline or `file:`), optional `doc_tags` |
| `help` | `help:<pkg.table>[/<resourceClass>]:<helpcode>` | `helper/*.xml` written by developers |
| `docu` | `docu:[<table>]:<hierarchical name>` | `docu.documentation` rst, served as a page of its own |

**Access**: never open. Only a registered calling page (`_calling_page_id`) of a logged, non-guest user; `doc_tags` on a grouplet card restricts it further. Forbidden → 403, unknown → 404.

**Responses**: `_fragment=1` → JSON `{title, html}` / `{title, page}` for the popup; otherwise a full HTML page (`sys/resources/ep_doc/doc_page_tpl.html`, or the rst2html page for docu).

**Template variables**: a grouplet doc is served as its template and filled **in the browser** on the card's data + `doc_kw` (the renderer the card already used): row values of a Bag-backed grid never leave the client and the source is cached once per page. The standalone page fills `doc_kw` and blanks the rest.

## Changes
- `gnrcomponents/externalcall:EndpointPermission` — the calling-page check `ep_table` had inline, now shared; `ep_table` uses it.
- `sys/webpages/ep_doc.py` (new).
- grouplet: a card/grid whose resource declares a doc now carries `doc_address` instead of the doc text (a caller's inline `doc=` and a custom `grouplets_root` stay inline); `_gr_resourceInfo` takes `pkg` for resources without a table.
- `genro.dlg.docUrl / docSource / docPopup / openDoc` (`genro_dlg.js`): one popup for the page (moved from `GroupletCard.showDoc`), styles moved to `09_gnr_dialogs_forms.css` as `.doc_popup_*`.
- `helperbutton`: a user's click now shows the help in that popup — before it read the value and showed nothing. The developer's in-place editing is unchanged.
- `docu.documentation.documentRst` shared by `docu/index/rst` and `ep_doc`.

## Pre-existing bugs fixed on the way
- `ep_table` tag check called `application.getResourcePermission`, which does not exist: any document with `readTags` raised `AttributeError`. Now `checkResourcePermission`.
- `saveHelperValue` did not create `helper/` for a table without one, so the first help of such a table could not be saved.

## Tests
- `gnrpy/tests/web/doc_endpoint_test.py` — real `GnrDummySite` on `gnrtest`: permissions (no page, unknown page, guest, `doc_tags` with real adm user/tag records), grouplet fragment and page, help saved through `saveHelperValue` and served escaped, 404s, the page-side profile carrying the address. Only the page register (daemon) is replaced.
- `docu/tests/test_docu_document_rst.py` — language fallback, placeholder, missing page (gnrdevelop db).
- `gnrjs/tests/doc_popup.test.js`, `grouplet_card.test.js` updated; `grouplet_card_test.py` updated for the address.
- flake8 clean; `gnrpy` pytest 3294 passed; JS 543 passed; test-page ratchets + docu package 99 passed.

Demo: `test/gnrwdg/test_doc_endpoint` (log in first: the endpoint never answers a guest).

## Not verified / limits
- In the browser only the guest path was checked (403 → "No documentation available", inline doc, helper popup, one fetch per address); the logged path is covered by the Python tests only.
- `docu:` through the endpoint is covered for "package not installed" only.
- `help:` on the endpoint reads the table package's own helper files; customization packages are not merged. Page-level help is not served: its save path is already broken (the page name is passed as a table).
- Out of scope, follow-ups: `saveHelperValue` has no developer check; non-TH help is saved to `helper/None.xml` but preloaded from `helper/default.xml`; `sys/docserver` reads `content_rst_*` columns no table has.

items.title: fix(clipboard,grouplet): a refused copy is reported; row tools sit side by side
items.body:
## Clipboard

`genro.textToClipboard` called `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with no error handling: a refused write (`NotAllowedError`) told the user nothing, and where `navigator.clipboard` is missing (plain http off localhost) the call raised.

- Outside a secure context it falls back to a hidden textarea + `execCommand('copy')` (as `gnr_tracebackviewer` already does).
- A failed copy shows an error `floatingMessage` ("Copy to clipboard failed"); the caller's message / callback runs only on success.
- The promise resolves to `true` / `false` and is never rejected.
- The core callers that wrote to `navigator.clipboard` directly now go through it: `genro_dom.copyInClipboard`, `gnrdomsource.copyInClipboard`, toast copy, form copy, grid `copyRows`.

## groupletGrid row tools

In struct mode with `delitem` and `editmenu` the trash was drawn over the kebab at the end of each row.

- The row tools take slots side by side from the right edge (`grouplet_grid_tool_slot_N`, set by the tile); in struct mode the row, header and footer reserve their room (`grouplet_grid--tools-2/3`), so columns stay aligned.
- New `copyitem=True` (`copyitem_kwargs`): Copy as an icon button out of the kebab, as `delitem` does for Delete. With `editmenu=True` the kebab then leaves Copy out. On cards with corner chrome the copy sits left of the trash; with the chrome band it stays in the band's kebab.

## Tests

- `gnrjs/tests/text_to_clipboard.test.js`: granted, refused, missing `navigator.clipboard`, failing fallback.
- `gnrjs/tests/grouplet_grid_phantom.test.js`: tool slots in struct rows and cards, copy button action.
- `gnrpy/tests/web/grouplet_card_test.py`: `copyitem` / `editmenu` resolution and the `--tools-N` flavour.
- Checked in the browser on `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/15_copy_paste` (new toggles for the delete and copy buttons): tools side by side, header aligned, a refused copy shows the error.

## Summary

Replace the inline dtype→widget mapping in `gnr.GroupletGridStructAdapter` with the canonical `genro.wdg.wdgByDtype` (and partially `widgetFromField`) helpers from `genro_wdg.js`.

## Objective

Align the struct adapter with the canonical framework path for resolving an editor widget from a column descriptor (`dtype`, `edit`, `related_table`, `values`, `format`, `validate_notnull`). Today the adapter has a private `_resolveWidgetTag` + `_editorKwargs` pair that reinvents what `widgetFromField` already does.

Risks of the current divergence: if Genropy adds a new dtype (e.g. duration, currency, geo) or changes a widget tag, the struct adapter silently falls behind because its mapping is hard-coded.

## Scope

In scope:

- `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet_grid.js`:
  - Replace the `_resolveWidgetTag` `dtype` map (lines ~241-247) with `genro.wdg.wdgByDtype(c.dtype)`.
  - Investigate whether `_editorKwargs` (lines ~250-270) can lean on `widgetFromField` for the `related_table → dbselect` and `values → filteringselect/combobox` branches (today they are reimplemented).
  - Keep groupletGrid-specific concerns local: the `grouplet_grid__struct_col_cell` marker class, the `value='^.field'` binding, `width:'100%'` default.

Out of scope:

- Changing the public API of `struct=` mode kwargs.
- Touching the resource= flow.

## Technical Details / Notes

Reference reading:

- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_wdg.js:210-222` — `wdgByDtype(dtype)` canonical mapping.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_wdg.js:224-248` — `widgetFromField(fieldattr)`, full editor resolution from a column descriptor.

The struct adapter's `_resolveWidgetTag` already mirrors `wdgByDtype` exactly (just with `Textbox` instead of `TextBox` as fallback — verify which case is canonical). The `_editorKwargs` is a superset of `widgetFromField` because it adds the marker class and the `^.field` binding; needs to be checked whether `widgetFromField`'s shape can be composed with our additions or if the duplication is justified.

One subtle difference: `widgetFromField` handles `wdg_*` and `validate_*` prefix extraction. The struct adapter does not (it expects already-extracted `edit` dict). If we want to consume `widgetFromField` directly we may need to pre-shape the input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_resolveWidgetTag` uses `genro.wdg.wdgByDtype(c.dtype)` for the dtype→tag map.
- [ ] If feasible, `_editorKwargs` consumes `widgetFromField` for related_table/values branches.
- [ ] test_9_struct_invoice and budget_editor render with the same widgets they render today.
- [ ] No widget tag regression (numeric → NumberTextBox, date → DateTextbox, bool → CheckBox, datetime → DatetimeTextbox).

## Dependencies

- None blocking.

items.title: feat(grouplet): groupletCard with its chrome band; grid drag opens a slot where the rows land
items.body:
A reusable card: a grouplet bound to a datapath with its chrome band. It is used alone (`pane.groupletCard(...)`, also as a roundedGroup in forms) and by `groupletGrid` for each card when `chromeSide` is set. Builds on the optional band of 5870b085e1.

**The card** — `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet_card.js`
- `gnr.GroupletCard`: band along top / left / right with tree chevron (▸ folded, ▾ open, animated), title, ⓘ doc, kebab, checkbox; the band is the drag source; folded, the card is its band; larger on coarse pointers.
- A field in error inside the card (open or folded) tints the band a very light red, distinct from the selection.
- Doc: one popup per page (`genro.dlg.quickTooltipPane`), Esc closes it; the doc is a template rendered on the card data with `doc_kw`, inline or `file:name.html` next to the resource (relative images made urls).
- `gnr.GroupletCardHost`: the card alone, state in the datastore.

**`groupletCard`** — `GroupletCardHandler.gr_groupletCard` in `grouplet.py`
- Without `resource`/`handler` it returns its body, like `roundedGroup` (same box look).
- Profile = resource `__info__` `card=dict(...)`, then caller kwargs: `chromeSide` (`'top'` default), `collapsible` (`False` default), `title`/`titleTemplate`/`titleField`, `emptyTitle`, `tools`, `doc`, `doc_kw`, `delitem`, `editmenu`. The resource `template` is the title of last resort.
- `collapsed='^.path'`, `checkbox='^.path'` keep the state in the page (resolved where the card is placed).
- `delitem`: `True` / `False` / `'^path'` / `'=path'` / `'==expr'` (over the card fields), read as the menu opens; alone, the entry clears the card's own fields (not the record around it).
- `useForm=True`: the grouplet in a `GroupletForm` of its own (autoSave 1, `form_*` kwargs), written back on save, reloaded with the form around the card (`_groupletPanel_innerReload`, flag path now a parameter).

**`groupletGrid`**
- With `chromeSide` each tile composes a `gnr.GroupletCard`; `collapsedTemplate` (else `titleTemplate`) is the band title, refreshed also while open.
- Card profile from the resource (per row with `resourceField`, via the template map) and `card_*` kwargs; dynamic `delitem` per row.
- Without `chromeSide` the corner chrome is unchanged (a test pins the kebab DOM the XOPXF CSS relies on).
- Missing template fields render blank instead of `undefined`.
- Whether a title is blank is read as text by `DOMParser` (no scripts run, no images load) instead of a tag-stripping regex, which CodeQL took for an incomplete sanitization (third commit; same results).
- Drag image of a card: drawn in a copy of its grid chain, above the page for the capture, at the card width (it was clipped and covered by the page).

**Drag opens a slot where the rows land** (second commit)
- Dragged rows lift out and leave a slot in their place; the slot follows the pointer, before or after the nearest row (rows by height, cards side by side by width); the rows around it slide aside (FLIP, 180ms). The drop lands in the slot (`<key` / `>key`; `moveRow` already took both).
- Dropped at home nothing moves; over no grid the slot goes back home; a drag ending nowhere, or Esc, puts the rows back.
- One slot per page: across grids sharing a `dragCode` (kanban), at the level that takes the drag in nested grids, at the tail over the add button or the blank row.
- Leaving a grid is told by a document `dragover`, not by `dragleave` (its `relatedTarget` is often null in Chromium: the slot bounced home and back); the slot holds still while rows slide.
- While the slot is open the row and grid under the pointer are not tinted (the framework `.canBeDropped` would); a refused drop still is. Tabs keep the insert-after drop. `prefers-reduced-motion`: slot without animations.

Not done: doc from a framework template address (`tpl:`); drag from a card alone; `useForm` inside the grid; the slot in the tabs strip.

Tests: `gnrjs/tests/grouplet_card.test.js` (18 cases) plus new cases in the grid tests, among them the slot (side, nearest row, whole drag, home, leave, lost drag; the DnD test surfaces get a minimal DOM); full JS suite 525/525. `gnrpy/tests/web/grouplet_card_test.py` (7 cases); Python suite green. cedi `tests/test_ddt_grid.py` passes against this branch.
Verified in the browser on `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_card` (cases 0–9) and `test_grouplet_grid/15_copy_paste` (band on three sides, fold, doc, clear, useForm write-back and reload, invalid tint) and regression pages 03, 08, 13 and `test_grouplets/06_grouplet_navigation`. Not checked live: the XOPXF budget editor and the teamset manual invoice (login); dark theme; Firefox. The new drag image was confirmed only by inspecting the element passed to `setDragImage`. The slot was checked with synthetic `DragEvent`s (cards, struct rows, kanban across grids, a pointer jittering on a border with null-`relatedTarget` dragleaves); by hand with the mouse on page 15 before the bounce fix (which is how the bounce was found), not again after it.

items.title: feat(doc): docs as Markdown in a documentation storage, edited in place by documenters
items.body:
Replaces #1731 (closed).

## What
**Experimental**: everything below is on only with `<experimental><gui inlinedoc="true"/></experimental>` in instanceconfig.xml. With the flag off nothing changes from `develop` (helper.xml, the helper editor, the inline card docs).

Documentation of fields, grouplets and pages lives as **MyST Markdown** files (YAML front matter: `id`, `title`, `type: reference`, `updated`, `author`) in the **`inlinedoc` storage**, a *private* storage: a folder of the instance (`<instance>/inlinedoc`) unless a storage service named `inlinedoc` is configured (siteconfig or the sys services, e.g. an S3 bucket in production). No url serves a private storage (`/_storage/inlinedoc/...` and `/inlinedoc:...` answer 404): only `sys/ep_doc` reads it. The code holds only the address, so updating a doc needs no rebuild or redeploy, and the same files can build the full Sphinx reference (myst-parser).

**Addresses** (context-sensitive help IDs, derived by convention):
| address | folder |
|---|---|
| `field:<pkg.table>:<column>` (every `field()`) | `<pkg>/<table>/fields/<column>/<lang>.md` |
| `grouplet:<pkg.table\|pkg>:<resource>` (cards, grid rows) | `<pkg>/<table>/grouplets/<resource>/` or `<pkg>/_grouplets/<resource>/` |
| `page:<pkg>/<page>:<helpcode>` (helpcode outside a table) | `<pkg>/_pages/<page>/<helpcode>/` |
| `table:<pkg.table>:`, `package:<pkg>:` | `<pkg>/<table>/_table/`, `<pkg>/_package/` |

Images go in `<folder>/assets/`. Language: the user's, then the db default, then `en`, then any.

**Who sees what**
- A page sends the addresses of its ⓘ icons to `sys/ep_doc` in **one request**; the server lists each table folder once (cached 30s, refreshed on save).
- Users see the ⓘ only where a doc exists.
- Documenters (`_DOC_,doc_<pkg>`) in **documentation mode** (`gnr.docModeVisible`, a menu line for `_DOC_`) also see the empty ones, red; a click opens the editor.
- The popup is a toggletip (click/Enter, Esc), with "Open in a new tab" and, for a documenter, **Edit**. The editor is `MDEditor` (ToastUI, wysiwyg) in a dialog; pasted images are stored next to the doc; a doc saved meanwhile by someone else answers 409 and the editor asks before overwriting.
- `sys/ep_doc` answers only a registered calling page of a logged, non-guest user, asked from that page's own connection; writing needs POST and the documenter tag `_DOC_,doc_<pkg>` of the doc's package, resolved server side. Rendering is markdown-it-py (CommonMark + tables) with raw HTML escaped: a doc cannot inject markup, and its title is escaped on the client. Uploaded images: png/jpeg/gif/webp only, checked on their bytes, 5 MB at most.

## Changes
- `gnr/web/gnrdocumentation.py` (new): addresses, front matter, rendering, `DocumentationStore`.
- `sys/webpages/ep_doc.py` (new) + `sys/resources/ep_doc/doc_page_tpl.html`.
- `StorageNode.file_mtimes()`: one paginated `list_objects_v2` on aws_s3, `os.walk` locally, a generic fallback on `children()`.
- `gnrcomponents/externalcall:EndpointPermission`, shared with `ep_table` (`same_connection=True` used by `ep_doc` only).
- Storage handler: `isPrivateStorage()` (`inlinedoc` by name, any storage with `private="true"`), refused by `storageDispatcher`; an unconfigured private storage falls back to the instance folder.
- `page.inlineDoc` (the experimental flag), `startArgs.inlineDoc` on the client.
- `genro_dlg.js`: `docTrack`, `docApplyStates`, `docSource`, `docPopup`, `openDoc`, `docEdit`, `docUploadImage`.
- `labledBox`: the ⓘ of a field / helpcode is the doc of its address; cards and grid rows use the same functions (`GroupletCard.docSpec` fills a grouplet doc's `$variables` with the row and offers them in the editor).
- **Replaced, with the flag on**: helper.xml (`saveHelperValue`, `getHelperData`, `setHelperData`, the developer prompt editor, `sys/helpeditor`, the "Open helper editor" menu lines) and the inline / `file:` HTML doc of grouplet cards: a card's `doc` is an address (`False` opts out, a legacy `file:` doc falls back to the resource's own address). With the flag off they all work as before.
- `markdown-it-py` added to the dependencies.

## Fixed on the way
- `ep_table`'s tag check called `application.getResourcePermission`, which does not exist: any document with `readTags` raised `AttributeError`.
- `funcApply` (gnrlang.js) failed on an action that is not written as `function(...)` (an arrow function): `match(...)[1]` of null.
- The ToastUI editor was loaded as `latest` from the CDN: pinned to editor 3.2.2, color picker v2.2.8, color-syntax plugin 3.0.3 (identical to today's `latest`).

## Tests
- `gnrpy/tests/web/gnrdocumentation_test.py`: real GnrDummySite on `gnrtest` with the flag on, docs in a real `inlinedoc` folder of the instance and in a configured `inlinedoc` service (a sys.service record), adm users and tags as records: addresses, front matter, rendering safety, listing (local and generic), index with language fallback and one listing per table, save/409/force, assets, endpoint permissions (no page, guest, another connection, documenter tag per package), no url serving the docs, a doc another worker wrote read at once, upload content and size, the endpoint off without the flag, fragment, page, index, save, upload. Replaced: the page register (daemon), the dummy request's HTTP method, boto's paginator for `aws_s3.file_mtimes`.
- `gnrjs/tests/doc_popup.test.js` (index in one request, icon states and documentation mode, popup, openDoc flows, editor save with relative images, 409, translation, image upload), `func_apply.test.js`, `grouplet_card.test.js` / `grouplet_grid_phantom.test.js` / `grouplet_card_test.py` updated.
- `grouplet_card_test.py` and `grouplet_card.test.js` cover both flag positions; `doc_popup.test.js` covers the escaped title.
- flake8 clean; gnrpy pytest 3335 passed, 21 skipped; JS 563 passed.

Demo: `test/gnrwdg/test_doc_storage` (flag on, log in; a user with `_DOC_` sees the editor).

## Not verified
- S3 for real (no bucket/minio here): `file_mtimes` on aws_s3 is tested with boto's paginator replaced.
- The rework after the review (flag, private storage, connection check, escaped title) was not tried in a browser nor over real HTTP.
- In the browser, before the review: reading (index, popup, Markdown table, per-row variables) and the editor dialog with a save refused 403 for a user without the tag. A real save from the browser by a documenter was not done (the test user had no `_DOC_`); it is covered by the Python and JS tests.

## Follow-ups (phase 2)
An atomic 409 (#1745); reference export to Sphinx from the inlinedoc storage; a coverage view for documenters; `aws_s3.versions()` matches by prefix and does not paginate.

items.title: feat(grouplet_grid): defaultRow ==expressions and additem_focus
items.body:
## What

Two groupletGrid options, needed by an editor that proposes the next account/chapter code and wants the caret on the name.

### `defaultRow` values as `==expression`

`defaultRowValues()` already read `=path` values when a row is made. It now also works out a `==expression` at that moment. As in `currentFromDatasource` / `GroupletCard.evaluateOn`, `this` is the grid's source node, and the expression receives `rows` (the grid's store Bag) and `grid` (the controller):

```python
defaultRow=dict(code='==xopxfEditor.nextCode(rows)', name='')
```

It applies wherever `defaultRowValues()` is read: `+` (add), the phantom blank row, the entry row reset, and paste. Each pasted row gets the next code, because the rows before it are already in the Bag.

A fresh phantom row left empty used to be compared with the defaults worked out again. With a `==` default that may differ (the next code), so such a row would no longer be dropped. A fresh row now records the defaults it was given (`_freshRows[key]`), and `_dropIfEmpty` measures against those.

### `additem_focus='<field>'`

After `+`, the caret goes to the editor bound to `^.<field>` in the new row instead of the first editor. Without the option nothing changes. A field that takes no typing (read-only, disabled) falls back to the first editor.

In lazy tabs (`lazyTabs=True`) the body is mounted in the next animation frame. The focus now waits for `mountBody()` and reads the tile's DOM at focus time, because the mount renders the wrapper anew. This also fixes a new lazy tab getting no focus at all, with or without the option.

## Tests

- `gnrjs/tests/grouplet_grid_options.test.js`:
  - a `==` default worked out at each add, over `rows`, `grid` and `this`, in the entry row and on paste;
  - a fresh row left empty is dropped, measured on its given defaults;
  - `additem_focus` on a field that is not the first, the fallback, a read-only field, and a lazy tab focusing once its body is mounted.
- `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 553/553 pass. The pre-commit hook (flake8 + Python suite) passed.
- New testhandler case `test_02_next_code` in `projects/gnrcore/packages/test/webpages/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/10_default_row.py`, with a code badge before the name, in cards and in lazy vtabs. Checked in the browser: `+` proposes 04004 after 04001–04003, and the caret lands on the name, in both layouts.

items.title: [TASK] groupletGrid: MVC store-ready — GroupletDataStore

labels.name: task
labels.description: Technical task, maintenance, or internal improvement

items.body:
## Sommario

Refactoring del controller `groupletGrid` in chiave MVC: il widget oggi mischia Model (accesso/mutazione della Bag) + View (rendering, DnD, layout). Introduciamo una classe **`GroupletDataStore`** come livello Model esplicito, con polimorfismo a tre modalità: `internal` (gestisce la Bag direttamente), `proxy` (delega a `gnr.stores.ValuesBagRows`), `adapter` (mappa da/verso store di forma diversa — `AttributesBagRows`, `Selection`, `RpcBase`).

## Documento di design

**[`docs/groupletgrid_store_integration.html`](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/feat-grouplet-grid/docs/groupletgrid_store_integration.html)** — riscritto in forma tabellare, contiene:

- Architettura a 3 mode (internal / proxy / adapter)
- Matrice completa delle API che `gnr.widgets.Grid` usa dallo store, con colonna "cosa facciamo noi" (Steal / Delegate / Adapt / Stub / Skip)
- Matrice dei punti di accesso diretto alla Bag nel controller attuale, con il nuovo wiring previsto
- Superficie pubblica di `GroupletDataStore` (Read, Mutate, Filter/Sort, Status/Lock, changeManager bridge)
- Dispatch table per mode (dove ogni API finisce in pratica)
- Fase 1 scope minimo con stub-with-warn pattern
- 9 rischi + 6 domande aperte

## Obiettivo

Il controller chiama solo `this.dataStore.X()`. Mai più `bag.getNodes()` o `popNode` diretti. Lo store esterno diventa un dettaglio del DataStore, non si propaga nei call site del widget.

## Fase 1 — scope minimo (proposta)

**Refactoring puro. Internal mode soltanto.** Test 1–12 invariati bit-per-bit. Le API non implementate fanno `console.warn` e ritornano default sensati.

| Step | Cosa |
|------|------|
| 1 | Creare classe `GroupletDataStore` (file separato), internal-only |
| 2 | Controller costruisce `this.dataStore` al init |
| 3 | Migrare `collectionStore()` literal → `this.dataStore` |
| 4 | Migrare iterazioni `bag.getNodes()` → `dataStore.visualOrder()` |
| 5 | Migrare mutazioni `popNode`/`setItem` → `dataStore.add/remove/move` |
| 6 | Migrare `_askAndDeleteRow` → `dataStore.deleteRowAsk()` |

**Out of scope Fase 1**: mode proxy, mode adapter, filter/sort UI, lock propagation, hasChanges/Errors reali, BagStore siblings emit lato Python.

## Pattern dei tre modes

```
GroupletDataStore (sempre presente, interna al controller)
   │
   ├─ mode "internal"   →   GnrBag diretta (default, nessuno store esterno)
   ├─ mode "proxy"      →   gnr.stores.ValuesBagRows (pass-through 1:1)
   └─ mode "adapter"    →   AttributesBagRows / Selection / RpcBase
                            (materializza Bag per i widget,
                             write-back via node.updAttributes)
```

L'adapter è il vero unlock: permette di puntare il `groupletGrid` a un `selectionStore` su tabella DB con righe attr-shaped, senza che il widget sappia che sotto non c'è una Bag values-shaped.

## Domande strategiche aperte

| # | Domanda | Quando |
|---|---------|--------|
| Q1 | `identifier` kwarg di primo livello su `gr_groupletGrid`? | Prima Fase 2 (proxy) |
| Q2 | Tag named (`pane.child('GroupletGrid', ...)`) o div + marker? | Prima Fase 2 |
| Q3 | `store_*` prefix come `bagGrid` o kwargs piatti? | Prima Fase 2 |
| Q4 | Mode proxy/adapter sono cittadini pieni o solo via `store_*` esplicito? | Prima Fase 2 |
| Q5 | DnD reorder in mode adapter su DB-backed: disabilitato o `_order` field? | Fase 3 / Item 14 |

items.title: fix(grouplet_grid): copied rows keep every row of their nested grids
items.body:
## Problem

Copying a groupletGrid row that holds a nested groupletGrid lost data on paste:

- A field of a nested row was named by its label. Labels repeat on every nested row (the fields of a popup `formlet` on each detail), so a card with 5 details wrote 5 columns all headed `Social charges rate`, and the paste put all five values on the first detail. Details 2–5 came back empty.
- The path of a nested field carried the nested row key (`Details.r_0.…`), and the columns were taken from one card only (`_firstRowFields`). A card with more details than the first card lost the extra ones, and a paste into a card with other keys or fewer details dropped them.

Separately, the selection bar computed `selection_menu.delete_locked` only when the selection changed: after unlocking the form with rows already selected, Delete stayed greyed out.

## Fix

In `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet_grid.js`:

- `_rowFields`: a field inside a row of a nested grid (a node with a `gridController`) goes by position, using Bag `#n` syntax (`details.#2.rate`, `details.#0.tags.#1.tag`), and is named by that path alone. All callers get this: copy, header matching, row paste, document paste.
- `_selectionTable` / `_copyFields(selection)`: the columns are the union of the fields of every selected row, for copy and for the Export Excel / Print presets alike.
- `_rowsFromText`: a header column with positions that the target row lacks is read by the same field of another row of the grid (`_gridFields`).
- `_insertPastedRows` / `_nestedKeys`: each `#n` resolves to the n-th nested row of the target, or to a new `r_…` key created in position order. A new nested row of an existing row is inserted with a trigger so its grid draws it (`updateRow` creates missing paths silently). A nested row made only of empty cells is not added.
- Selection bar kebab: `connect_onmousedown` re-reads the bar (count, label, `delete_locked`), as the row kebab already does with `_refreshRowMenu`.

Nested struct grids inside a popup (e.g. tag lists) round-trip too. Their rows are built even before the popup is first opened.

Known limit: a pasted nested row gets the copied values, not the nested grid's `defaultRow`.

## Tests

- `gnrjs/tests/grouplet_grid_phantom.test.js`: nested rows named by position with each popup field kept apart; a paste back as new rows and over a row with fewer nested rows (existing key kept, tags included); the selection bar re-reading `delete_locked` when its menu opens.
- `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 553/553 pass (rebased on develop). The pre-commit hook (flake8 + Python suite) passed.
- New testhandler case `test_04_nested` in `projects/gnrcore/packages/test/webpages/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/15_copy_paste.py`: cards with a grid of details, each with fields in a `tooltipPane` + `formlet` and a struct grid of tags in the popup. Checked in the browser: the copy names every popup field per detail, and pasting as new cards or over a card with one detail restores all 3 details with rate, phase and tags, and draws them. The Delete re-read is covered by the unit test only, since that page has no lockable form.

## Checklist

- [x] flake8 passes on modified Python files
- [x] JS tests pass
- [x] No unused imports
- [x] Logic in the library code, test page only wires the case

items.title: [FEATURE] Choice tiles widget for grouplet wizard steps
items.body:
## Summary
A reusable "choice tiles" widget for grouplets, usable as a self-advancing wizard step.

## Problem or Need
Applications build "pick one of N" wizard steps by hand (Teamset's manual invoice type step): a `lightButton` per tile setting the record field and calling `gnr_grouplet.wizardNext` with a frameCode derived from the step form id, a `dataController` per tile for the selected class, a hidden notnull field to keep the step invalid, app CSS for the tiles and a `:has()` rule to hide the wizard's Next button.

## Proposed Solution
- `@struct_method gr_groupletChoice(pane, field, table/columns/where/order_by (+ query params) or rows, value_column='pkey', glyph, title, note, caption_field, groups, autoNext=True)`: tiles bound to `^.<field>`; `glyph`/`title`/`note` as a column, a `$template` or a callable; `groups` = list of `dict(caption, condition, _class)`; a click sets the field (and the caption field) and, inside a wizard step, advances it; a hidden notnull field keeps the step invalid until chosen.
- Wizard: a grouplet `__info__` key `autoNext=True` hides the Next button on that step.
- Tile CSS in `grouplet.css` on the theme variables.
- Demo page under `test/webpages/gnrwdg/test_grouplets/`.

## Impact and Scope
`gnrcomponents/grouplet` (py, js, css) and the test package. Teamset's type step reduces to one call (adopted separately).

items.title: fix(localization): keep a section per file for modules sharing a basename
items.body:
Fixes #1402

## Problem

`_updateModuleLocalization` named each module's section after its path without the extension, so `grouplet.py` and `grouplet.js` shared the section `resources.common.gnrcomponents.grouplet.grouplet` and the `.py` (scanned second) overwrote the `.js`. At every regeneration of `localization.xml` the `.js` keys disappeared, and their translations were lost at the one after.

## Change

When the section path is already taken, it is suffixed with the file extension (`grouplet_py`), following the `DirectoryResolver.makeLabel` convention. Sections that do not collide keep their current label, so a regeneration does not rename the existing sections. No migration is needed: `updateLocalizationDict` and `translateBlock` read only the leaf keys, never the section labels.

## Verification

- New test `test_same_basename_modules_keep_their_sections` (real `AppLocalizer`, temporary folder, real `updateLocalizationFiles`): fails without the fix (`assert 'py' == 'js'`), passes with it.
- Regeneration of the core slot on a copy of the sources: the `grouplet` (js) and `grouplet_py` sections are both present. Without the fix the js section is missing.
- flake8 clean on the touched files; full suite: 2969 passed, 21 skipped.

items.title: [FEATURE] groupletPanel: mandatory grouplets marked in the menu and blocking the outer form
items.body:
## Summary

A grouplet can declare in `__info__` the fields it requires (`mandatory='field_a,field_b'`); groupletPanel marks its menu entry with a mandatory icon until they are filled, and the outer form stays invalid meanwhile.

## Problem or Need

In a groupletPanel only the grouplet currently open is validated (its inner form). A required group the user never opens gives no signal and does not block the outer save: the record can be saved incomplete, and nothing in the tree or multibutton tells the user which groups still have to be filled.

## Proposed Solution

- `__info__` of a grouplet returns `mandatory='field_a,field_b'`: paths relative to the grouplet location (with `locationpath='record'` they are record columns). `_buildGroupletMenu` already copies `__info__` onto the menu node attributes, so the list reaches the client with the menu.
- groupletPanel evaluates completeness on the data, not on the built grouplet: a group is complete when none of its `mandatory` paths is blank (`isNullOrBlank`) under the panel `value`. It runs when the outer form loads and on every change under `value`, so it also covers groups never opened.
- While a group is incomplete its menu label (tree node and multibutton button) shows a mandatory marker: an SVG icon through a CSS class in `grouplet.css`, removed when the group is complete.
- The outer form is invalid while any mandatory group is incomplete, via the existing form error API: `form.setFormError('grouplet_<code>', <message>, false)` on the panel's `#FORM`, cleared with `setFormError(code, false)`; `isValid()` already accounts for `formErrors`. The message names the group caption, e.g. "Complete <caption>".
- A topic node shows the marker when any of its children is incomplete.

## Considered Alternatives

- An `isComplete(data)` callback in `__info__`: more flexible, but code per grouplet for the common case of required fields.
- Deriving the required fields by building each grouplet server-side and collecting `validate_notnull`: automatic, but costly and it misses conditional rules.
- Relying on the open inner form's validity only: does not cover groups never opened (the current behaviour).

## Impact and Scope

groupletPanel (tree and multibutton) in `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/`. Benefits the adm preferences and the client pages that edit a record through `locationpath='record'` grouplets (anaci Impostazioni on groupletPanel). No change for grouplets without `mandatory`.

## Additional Information

Builds on the groupletPanel fixes of #1464 / #1465 (inner form on a whole record, pkey at `.pkey`).

items.title: [BUG] Mixin metadata mutation corrupts already-bound RPC names and breaks nested GroupletGrid templates
items.body:
## Problem Description

`classMixin` and `instanceMixin` mutate RPC routing metadata on shared Python function objects. Loading or mixing another resource can therefore change the serialized RPC identity of a method that is already bound to a different page/resource.

In the observed nested GroupletGrid flow, this produces a template response containing a **bare** `gr_getGroupletGridTemplate` loader instead of its resource-qualified name. The browser then calls that bare method, receives HTTP 200 with a top-level GenRoBag RPC error, and leaves one nested detail grid absent:

```text
[GG] template RPC failed missing handler: gr_getGroupletGridTemplate
```

**Expected:** once a callable has been bound to a page/resource, subsequent class or instance mixins must not erase or replace its RPC qualification. Every nested grid must load its template successfully.

**Observed:** the original bound method retains its `self`, but its underlying function's `__mixin_pkg` / `__mixin_path` are overwritten. The defect can both remove qualification and redirect an existing method to another resource. The missing-grid failure is intermittent; the underlying metadata corruption is deterministic and reproducible without concurrency.

## Reproduction Steps

### Deterministic framework-only reproduction

Run this in a fresh Python process with the affected GenroPy `gnrpy` on `PYTHONPATH`. No site, database, authentication, customer data or browser is required. This exact script was executed successfully against the affected runtime; its assertions verify the current broken behavior.

```python
from gnr.core.gnrdecorator import public_method
from gnr.core.gnrlang import (
    GnrObject, classMixin, instanceMixin, serializedFuncName,
)

class SharedHandler:
    @public_method
    def template(self):
        return 'template'

class AccountResource(SharedHandler):
    pass

setattr(AccountResource, '__mixin_path', 'repro/account:AccountResource')
page = GnrObject()
instanceMixin(page, AccountResource)
held = page.template
before = serializedFuncName(held)

class ItemResource:
    pass

# Building another resource class clears the shared function's routing metadata.
classMixin(ItemResource, SharedHandler)
after_class_mixin = serializedFuncName(held)
shared = held.__func__ is ItemResource.template

# Binding that resource elsewhere also rewrites the original held method's route.
setattr(ItemResource, '__mixin_path', 'repro/item:ItemResource')
other_page = GnrObject()
instanceMixin(other_page, ItemResource)
after_instance_mixin = serializedFuncName(held)

print('before:', before)
print('after classMixin:', after_class_mixin)
print('shared function:', shared)
print('after other instanceMixin:', after_instance_mixin)

assert before == '*|repro/account:AccountResource;template'
assert after_class_mixin == 'template'
assert shared is True
assert after_instance_mixin == '*|repro/item:ItemResource;template'
```

Actual output:

```text
before: *|repro/account:AccountResource;template
after classMixin: template
shared function: True
after other instanceMixin: *|repro/item:ItemResource;template
```

For a regression test, the invariant should instead be `serializedFuncName(held) == before` after **both** subsequent operations. That invariant currently fails.

### Actual resource-loader reproduction

The same loss was also reproduced with the existing `GnrWsgiSite` resource loader:

1. `mixinPageComponent(page, 'grouplets/bd_edit/account:Grouplet')`.
2. Hold `page.gr_getGroupletGridTemplate`; its serialized name is `*|grouplets/bd_edit/account:Grouplet;gr_getGroupletGridTemplate`.
3. Call `loadResource('grouplets/bd_edit/item:Grouplet', page=page)`; the item's `py_requires` includes `GroupletGridHandler`.
4. Serialize the already-held method again: it is now bare `gr_getGroupletGridTemplate`.
5. The new component's template method and the held method have the same `__func__`.

This probe used actual loader APIs with no framework patch or database writes. The application resources are needed only for this second reproduction; the framework-only script above is self-contained.

### Browser reproduction

In a local Teamset project form, inside its normal table-handler iframe:

1. Import an XOPXF document with one chapter, four accounts, one item per account and one detail per item.
2. Open the nested editor through the native **Apri editor** action. Its hierarchy uses existing resource-based GroupletGrid APIs: chapter → account → item → detail.
3. Close the editor, return through the root menu into a fresh project frame and open the editor again.
4. Observe the template RPC error and three rendered detail rows instead of four.

Two initial mounts loaded all four details. The fresh-frame opening reproduced the failure on 2026-10-14 at 07:58:49 UTC. This is an intermittent browser reproduction, not a guarantee that every opening fails. The affected case was stopped before Save, Confirm or any transfer.

## Environment

- GenroPy runtime: [`c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf`](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/commit/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf), including the delivered #1613 work. That reference identifies the tested build; it does not attribute this defect to #1613.
- The isolated runtime's `gnrlang.py`, `gnrresourceloader.py`, `grouplet.py` and `grouplet_grid.js` were verified byte-identical to that commit. Public served `grouplet_grid.js` and `genro_components.js` matched the runtime files.
- Python 3.13.2; macOS 27.0 (26A428); installed Chrome 155.0.8059.40.
- Local `teamset_apps` multidb instance with disposable fixtures; no schema migration. Schema check returned `STRUCTURE OK`.
- No application or framework source correction has been applied.

## Additional Material

### The malformed loader is already in the server response

Sanitized metadata from the captured test interval:

| UTC timestamp | Event | Observed binding/result |
|---|---|---|
| 07:58:49.239 | Qualified account-template request | Response emits `loaderrpc="gr_getGroupletGridTemplate::RPC"` and `mapLoaderrpc="gr_getGroupletGridTemplateMap::RPC"` |
| 07:58:49.241–.242 | Neighboring qualified account-template requests | Responses emit `*|grouplets/bd_edit/item:Grouplet;gr_getGroupletGridTemplate::RPC` and the corresponding qualified map loader |
| 07:58:49.304 | Browser dispatches emitted bare loader | POST method `gr_getGroupletGridTemplate`; HTTP 200 with top-level RPC error |
| 07:58:49.343 | Console callback | `[GG] template RPC failed missing handler: gr_getGroupletGridTemplate` |

The error envelope contains:

```xml
<GenRoBag>
  <error>missing handler: gr_getGroupletGridTemplate</error>
  <result _T="NN"></result>
</GenRoBag>
```

The captured interval contains 263 local test requests, one top-level RPC error and no HTTP/network failures. HTTP status alone therefore misses the functional failure. Raw authenticated HAR and customer screenshots are intentionally not attached; the relevant sanitized evidence is included above.

### Verified mechanism and source references

All links below are pinned to the tested build:

- [`classMixin`, gnrlang.py:446–461](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf/gnrpy/gnr/core/gnrlang.py#L446-L461) reads metadata from the source class and assigns `proxy_name`, `__mixin_pkg` and `__mixin_path` directly on the reused function, including `None`.
- [`instanceMixin`, gnrlang.py:568–585](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf/gnrpy/gnr/core/gnrlang.py#L568-L585) unwraps `method.__func__`, creates `MethodType(method, obj)`, then annotates that same function. The proxy-class branch also mutates callable metadata.
- [`serializedFuncName`, gnrlang.py:487–506](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf/gnrpy/gnr/core/gnrlang.py#L487-L506) reads those mutable attributes when constructing the RPC name.
- [`GnrClassCatalog`, gnrclasses.py:366](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf/gnrpy/gnr/core/gnrclasses.py#L366) registers this serializer for bound methods.
- [`ResourceLoader`, gnrresourceloader.py:534–577](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf/gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwsgisite_proxy/gnrresourceloader.py#L534-L577) builds resource classes with mixins before attaching resource qualification to the component and mixing it into the page.
- [`GroupletGrid`, grouplet.py:1350–1351](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf/resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.py#L1350-L1351) passes the bound loader methods into the emitted controller. [`grouplet_grid.js:3334–3339`](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/blob/c6a83a803dc5842229ae84d2269c10926dc6aeaf/resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet_grid.js#L3334-L3339) dispatches the emitted name and reports the RPC error.

The deterministic probes establish shared-function mutation. The observed browser responses establish that lost qualification reaches the client. The specific thread scheduling was not instrumented; interleaved resource loading/serialization explains the intermittent manifestation without being required for the framework-only reproduction.

### Suggested correction and acceptance criteria

Correct the shared mixin/binding machinery so RPC identity belongs to the individual binding and cannot be rewritten by later resource/class/instance construction. Copying callable objects before annotating them is one candidate implementation; it has not been implemented or validated. Avoid introducing a new RPC API or a GroupletGrid/application-specific workaround.

- Add deterministic regression tests, starting in `gnrpy/tests/core/gnrlang_test.py`, that keep an earlier bound method qualified after both an unqualified `classMixin` and a differently qualified `instanceMixin`.
- Cover two distinct resource paths and package qualifications, including inherited handlers and the proxy mixin path. Inspect related web resource-loader tests and cover actual `loadResource`/`mixinPageComponent` behavior.
- Preserve callable behavior, decorator flags, defaults/closures, proxy routing, existing prefix/suffix/mangling conventions and overridden-method backups.
- Verify that concurrent nested template responses retain correct `loaderrpc` and `mapLoaderrpc` values.
- Recheck the native editor with all four detail grids mounted, edit and Save, then close/reopen through the root menu. Preserve the complete document, anchor and hidden metadata, with no template RPC/console failure.

### Validation boundary

The local application's full XOPXF suite passed **107 tests**; targeted lint on six relevant unchanged files returned zero. These are baseline results, not proof of a fix. The single disposable fixture and temporary flag/storage changes were cleaned/restored through ORM hooks, with independent readback; the dedicated runtime was stopped.

A separately recorded `undefined.forEach` error did not recur in this limited run and remains unresolved. No causal link between that error and this mixin defect has been demonstrated. No repaired Save/persistence or full application acceptance is claimed by this issue.
