items.title: feat(doc): the "?" opens the published manual's section in a help panel
items.body:
Stacked on #1736 (base `feature/doc-storage`): it retargets to `develop` once #1736 is merged.

## What
The published user manual — a Sphinx + myst-parser site, as the applications' manuals already are (demetra, icond2) — becomes the main source of the in-app help. The customer's notes of #1736 stay next to it.

**The link: the doc address is the help ID, the manual declares it.** A section documents a UI element when a label made from the element's address sits above it:

```
field:invc.invoice:customer_id   ->  (help-field-invc-invoice-customer_id)=
table:invc.invoice:              ->  (help-table-invc-invoice)=
grouplet:test:card_profile       ->  (help-grouplet-test-card_profile)=
page:demetra/agenda:giornata     ->  (help-page-demetra-agenda-giornata)=
```

A label is unique in a Sphinx site, and one site may hold several profile manuals (demetra: operatore, backoffice di sede, backoffice generale): a variant suffix lets each document the same element, `(help-field-...--operatore)=`. Sphinx writes the labels to `objects.inv`, the map read here: no hand-kept file, build and publishing unchanged.

**Which manual: the existing adm.helpdoc.** The manuals a user reaches are the `adm.helpdoc` pages linked to the group the user logged in with (`adm.group_helpdoc`, the same records the frameindex Help menu lists), then the helpdocs linked to no group. The user's own pages decide between variants, then the label without variant. A helpdoc url can be an http(s) url, a file, or a local storage path of the site (`site:manual/index.html`), read as a file and linked at its storage url, for a manual the instance serves itself.

## Changes
- `gnr/web/gnrmanual.py` (new): `address_label`, `parse_inventory` (Sphinx v2 inventory, stdlib zlib), `site_of` (the `objects.inv` of a page, its folder then the ones above), `cut_section` (lxml: the section the label opens; links and images absolute; scripts, iframes, `on*` attributes, `javascript:` links and header links dropped), `Manual` (cached fetch, TTL 300s).
- `sys/ep_doc`: the page index also lists the addresses with a manual section; the fragment carries `manual: {label, url, title, html}`.
- `genro.dlg.helpPanel` replaces the doc popup of #1736: a panel on the right of the page with the manual's section, **Open in the manual** (a window of its own, `gnr_manual`, reused by the next link; the page stays), then the customer's note with Edit / Add a note for a documenter; close button or Esc. The icon shows when the manual or a note documents the address.
- Hosts: `docHelpButton` (GnrDomSrc); the page top bar (`pageHelp`: `table:<maintable>:` for a page of a table, `page:<pkg>/<page>:` otherwise); `roundedGroup` / `roundedGroupFrame` with `helpcode`; the toolbar of a table handler view that is not the page's (`vhelp`) and of a form of another table (`form_help`); fields and grouplet cards already had it.
- Demo: `test/gnrwdg/test_manual_help` and a small manual in `test/docs/manual` (a button builds it with Sphinx and links it as an adm.helpdoc).

## Tests
- `gnrpy/tests/web/gnrmanual_test.py`: a real Sphinx + myst-parser build (skipped where Sphinx is not installed: it is not a genropy dependency), read from the build folder and over a real local HTTP server: labels, inventory, site discovery, variants and preference, section cut (scripts, absolute images, next chapter excluded), cache and expiry.
- `gnrdocumentation_test.py`: through `sys/ep_doc` with real adm records (group, users, helpdocs, group_helpdoc): the grouped user gets its own variant, a user of no group the plain label, index and fragment.
- `gnrjs/tests/doc_popup.test.js`: icon states with the manual, the panel (manual, link in its own window, note, Edit / Add a note, Esc, close), openDoc flows.
- flake8 clean; gnrpy pytest green in the commit hook; JS 563 passed; test-page ratchets green.

## Checked in the browser
On `test/gnrwdg/test_manual_help` (manual built and linked as `site:_demo_manual/users.html`): the "?" shows for username, email, the card, the Shipping block and the adm.user view, not for firstname (no section); each opens its section; Open in the manual answers 200 at the section's anchor; on `/sys/thpage/adm/user` the "?" of the page top bar opens the table's section, the nested table handlers without section show none.

## Not verified
- A separate browser window: the app's embedded browser has no popups (`window.open` returns null there); the click keeps the page and calls `genro.openWindow(url, 'gnr_manual')`, checked.
- A manual on a private host: the server fetch has no credentials; a private manual can be served by the instance through a storage path.
- The demetra / icond2 manuals carry no `help-` labels yet: they are added when the manuals are next updated.

items.title: [BUG] wizardConfirm leaves the record flagged as confirmed when the save does not run
items.body:
## Problem Description

`gnr_grouplet.wizardConfirm` (`resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.js`) calls `mainForm.setDraft(false)`, sets `.wizard_confirming`, then `mainForm.save({always: true})`, and rolls both back only when `save()` returns a string (refused as invalid). `save()` can also return without saving and without a string:

- `undefined` when a grid editor is still open (`checkPendingGridEditor`: the save is deferred through `sourceNode.watch`);
- `false` when `opStatus` is already set (another save or load in progress).

In those cases the record stays with `__is_draft` false and `wizard_confirming` true; if the deferred save then fails (e.g. server-side), only `formsubscribe_onSaveFailed` can restore it.

## Expected

The confirm marks the record only for a save that actually starts, or rolls back on every outcome that is not a started save.

## Environment

genropy develop. Found by reading the code; not reproduced in the browser.

items.title: [BUG] Localization scanner drops the section of a module sharing its basename with another file (grouplet.py / grouplet.js)
items.body:
### Problem Description

`AppLocalizer._updateModuleLocalization` (`gnrpy/gnr/app/gnrlocalization.py`) stores the strings of each scanned module under a section named after the module path **without its extension**. Two modules in the same folder with the same basename and different extensions (e.g. `grouplet.py` and `grouplet.js`) map to the same section, and the second one scanned (`.py`, files are walked in sorted order) overwrites the first.

After a regeneration of `localization.xml` the `.js` module's keys disappear from the file; at the following regeneration they come back with only their base text, so their translations are lost.

Expected: every scanned file keeps its own section, and its keys and translations survive a regeneration.

In core, 10 folders currently hold a `.py`/`.js` pair where both files carry localizable strings (`frameindex`, `th_groupth`, `dashboard_component`, `statspane`, `batch_handler`, `chartjs`, `login`, `th`, `reporthandler`, `grouplet`). Only `grouplet.js` has a section in `localization.xml`, and only because it was added by hand.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Put two modules in one folder: `grouplet.js` containing `'!!Please complete required fields'` and `grouplet.py` containing `'!!Save draft'`.
2. Regenerate the localization file (`AppLocalizer.updateLocalizationFiles`).
3. Open the resulting `localization.xml`: only the `grouplet.py` section is there, `en_please_complete_required_fields` is gone.

### Environment

`develop` at 1b76b3c68; independent of OS and browser (server-side scanner).

### Additional Material

Proposed fix: when the section path is already taken, suffix it with the file extension (`grouplet_py`), following the `DirectoryResolver.makeLabel` convention. Existing files need no migration: `updateLocalizationDict` reads only the leaf keys, never the section labels.

items.title: grouplet wizard: saves only through its own steps
items.body:
Fixes #1496
Fixes #1498
Fixes #1499

## Pending changes dialog (#1496)
Closing a `groupletWizardForm` with unsaved changes offered **Save**, which stored the record without going through the remaining steps. `openPendingChangesDlg` now honours the form option `pendingChangesSaveSlot` (set as `form_pendingChangesSaveSlot`, like `form_avoidPendingChangesDialog`); `false` removes the Save button and also stops Shift on a dismiss from saving silently in `load_store`. `groupletWizardForm` sets it to `False`.

## Back on an incomplete step
`wizardGoTo` (32059a9d8c, on develop) saved an incomplete step by forcing `form.allowSaveInvalid = true` around `form.save()` and resetting it to `false` right after:
- with a grid editor still open, `save()` defers itself through `sourceNode.watch` and runs after the reset, so the step was refused as invalid and its changes dropped;
- the reset clobbered a configured `allowSaveInvalid`.

The step form now declares `form_allowSaveInvalid=True` and Back just calls `form.save()`. Validity is still enforced by the wizard on Next and on Confirm (`wizardNext`, `wizardConfirm` check `isValid()` before saving).

## Closing with unsaved step changes (#1498)
The step form was never registered in the surrounding form's `childForms`, so `GnrFrmHandler.load()` (the `childForms` loop before a dismiss) did not see its changes: after a Next, closing the dialog dropped the current step's edits without a prompt. The step form now registers itself on every build (`gnr_grouplet.wizardRegisterStep`, run from `GroupletForm`'s `_onRemote`, same idiom as `th.py:797`) and declares `form_pendingChangesSaveSlot=False`: the dismiss shows Pending changes with Discard and Cancel only, titled with the parent's record.

## Confirm that does not start a save (#1499)
`wizardConfirm` cleared the draft flag and rolled it back only when `save()` returned a string. A save that never started (form busy, blocked, `onSaving` interruption) left `__is_draft` false and `wizard_confirming` set. Confirm now does nothing while `opStatus` is set, and restores the draft whenever no save is under way after the call; a save under way still ends in `onSaved` / `onSaveFailed`.

## Tests
`gnrjs/tests/wizard_save_paths.test.js` (real `genro_frm.js`, `grouplet.js`, and `genro_components.js` for `GroupletForm`):
- Pending changes option: dialog slots with and without it, an explicit `saveSlot` argument still decides, Shift on a dismiss, an `autoSave` form still saves.
- Back: a changed step is saved at once whether valid or not, an unchanged one is not, a pending grid editor defers the save without losing it.
- Registration (#1498): the step form built by the real `GroupletForm` runs the `_onRemote` hook passed by `groupletWizard` (read from `grouplet.py`), registers in the parent's `childForms`, takes its `table_name` and still loads; the hook runs next to another remote hook declaring the same names; no parent form is a no-op; a rebuilt step replaces the old one.
- Dismiss through a registered step: Cancel stays, Discard closes once; an untouched step closes without asking.
- Confirm (#1499): a save that does not start, a busy form, a save under way, a save completing at once, a save deferred by a grid editor (stays a draft), a changed step saved first, an invalid step blocking.

`gnrjs/tests/item_formstore_record.test.js`: `_invalidFields` set on the item form's record is not carried to the destination record and is gone after the item form reloads.

Against the code before each fix: the #1496 cases fail on develop, the registration/dismiss/Confirm cases fail on 657b4398ce, the sibling-hook case fails with a hook declaring `const frm` inline.

- `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 196 passed; Python suite green (pre-commit on the source commits); flake8 clean on `grouplet.py`.
- Browser, `test_grouplets/06_grouplet_navigation` → `test_11_wizard_resume`: a draft row with the mandatory qty empty survives Back → Next; Pending changes offers Discard and Cancel only; with changes in the current step after a Next, closing asks (Cancel keeps the row, Discard closes); after Back on an incomplete step the wizard's record carries no `_invalidFields`; Complete Ticket confirms, locks and offers Back to draft.

items.title: [FEATURE] groupletGrid totals: a row count entry and hidden= per entry
items.body:
## Summary

Two additions to the `groupletGrid` totals band (`totals=`): a row count entry, and a `hidden=` per entry.

## Problem or Need

- The band can only sum a row field (`field=`) or compute a formula over the other totals (`name=` + `formula=`): there is no way to show how many rows the grid holds.
- `totals_hidden` hides the whole band. A document grid whose money totals make sense only for some documents (a DDT: priced on a sale, not on a transfer) cannot keep the row count visible while hiding the money.

## Proposed Solution

- `dict(name='righe', count=True, label='Righe')`: the number of rows, kept current on row insert/delete and on a new datastore.
- Every entry accepts `hidden=` plus its dynamic parameters (e.g. `hidden='==causale!="VENDITA"', causale='^#FORM.record.causale_trasporto'`), applied to that entry's cell; `totals_hidden` keeps hiding the whole band.

## Impact and Scope

`resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.py` (`_gr_groupletGrid_totals`) and `grouplet_grid.js` (totals band). Existing `totals=` declarations are unchanged.

items.title: feat(grouplet): a row count and hidden= per entry in the groupletGrid totals
items.body:
Fixes #1473

Two additions to the `groupletGrid` totals band (`totals=`), backward compatible with existing declarations:

- **Row count**: `dict(name='righe', count=True, label='Righe')` shows the number of rows, updated on row insert/delete (`gnr_storepath`) and on every `newDataStore` (a record with no rows Bag counts 0). The band's `totals_format` does not apply to a count; formulas over the totals can read it.
- **Attributes per entry**: every key of an entry that is not one of its own (`field`, `name`, `formula`, `count`, `label`, `format`, `highlight`) goes to that entry's cell. So `hidden=` with its dynamic parameters hides a single entry; an entry `_class` is appended to the cell's own. `totals_hidden` keeps hiding the whole band.

- `gnrjs/tests/grouplet_grid_totals.test.js` (new, fails without the change); the whole `gnrjs/tests` suite passes (174/174).

items.title: [BUG] A failed build in the source trigger queue freezes every later build of the page
items.body:
### Problem Description

On a page with many dynamic components, one failed build in the source trigger queue freezes every later build of the page.

`GnrSrcHandler.nodeTrigger` (`gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_src.js`) queues the source triggers that arrive while a build is running and drains them with `pop()`, last in first out. Two nested inserts queued together — a parent and then a child added into it, as `genro.dom.makeHiderLayer` does for a remote pane's waiting message — are built child first: the child finds no destination ("Missing destination node in trigger_ins") and `makeDomNode` throws on `destination.containerNode`. The exception leaves the loop with `genro.src.building` still `true`, so from then on every source change of the page is queued and never built.

On `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplets/06_grouplet_navigation` loaded in full, a groupletWizard moves its stepper on Next and changes `.current_resource`, but the step pane keeps the previous step's fields (the new step's source is in the tree, never built), or stays empty from the start. The wizards inside the dialogTableHandlers (test_4/5/11/12) are frozen the same way.

How the queue gets nested inserts here: a widget built inside the loop calls `_T()`, whose `getRemoteTranslation` is a synchronous rpc; dojo delivers the already completed async responses during it (the `dataRpc` of test_9), so their data triggers run with `building` true. The MultiButton's `makeButtons` selects its first item, a dataController changes the resource of a remote `grouplet`, and `updateRemoteContent` adds the hider layer inside the running loop.

Related defects on the same path:
- `_trigger_upd` on a node still queued for insertion falls back to the first built ancestor's DOM and replaces it.
- `GnrDomSourceNode.build` leaves `_isBuilding` true when the build throws, and `nodeTrigger` ignores that node's triggers forever.
- MultiButton `setValue` reads `n.domNode` of buttons still queued (`isElementOverflowing` throws on `parentElement`) and its `setClass` falls back to the container.

Expected: a queued child is built by its parent's build, a failed build does not stop the queue, and the page keeps building.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Open `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplets/06_grouplet_navigation` with all tests (no `/N` filter). Reload a few times: it happens on about one load in five, depending on the arrival order of the async responses.
2. In the console: `genro.src.building` is `true` and `genro.src.pendingBuild.length` is in the hundreds.
3. Click Next on a groupletWizard: the stepper moves, the step pane does not change.

### Environment

genropy `develop` (bf7029daf7), sandboxpg instance, Chrome.

### Additional Material

Console on a frozen load:
```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parentElement')    // MultiButton setValue
Missing destination node in trigger_ins {evt: ins, ...}          // div inside hiderNode
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'containerNode')    // makeDomNode
trigger index: subscription of a discarded source node textbox value gnr.grouplet_<frameCode>_step_form.record.contact_name
```

items.title: fix(gnrjs): a failed build in the source trigger queue no longer freezes the page
items.body:
Fixes #1507

## Problem

`GnrSrcHandler.nodeTrigger` drains the source triggers queued during a build last in first out. A parent and a child inserted into it while a build runs — the hider layer of a remote pane with its waiting message — were built child first: the child had no destination, `makeDomNode` threw, and the exception left `genro.src.building` set. From then on every source change of the page was queued and never built: on the full `06_grouplet_navigation` page a groupletWizard moved its stepper on Next while its step pane kept the previous step (or stayed empty), and the wizards in the dialogTableHandlers were frozen too.

The nested inserts reach the queue through a re-entry: `_T()` makes a synchronous rpc during a build, dojo delivers the completed async responses inside it, and their triggers (a `dataRpc` filling a MultiButton, which selects a remote `grouplet`) run with `building` set.

## Changes

- `genro_src.js`: a child whose parent, or an ancestor, is still queued for insertion waits for that build, which builds it with the parent's content; the same for an update of a node still queued (`getDomNode` would hand over the first built ancestor to be replaced).
- `genro_src.js`: a failed queued trigger neither stops the queue nor leaves `building` set: its error is rethrown on its own (`setTimeout`), so it stays an uncaught error with its original stack. Rethrowing it to the caller would skip the caller's own cleanup (`_releaseRemoteUpdate` after `mergeRemoteContent`), and the caller is often not the one that queued the failed build.
- `gnrdomsource.js`: `GnrDomSourceNode.build` releases `_isBuilding` when the build throws; left set, `nodeTrigger` ignored that node for good.
- `genro_components.js`: MultiButton `setValue` skips the buttons still queued for build (`n.domNode` missing; `setClass` would fall back to the container). `oneButton` creates them with the right class.

Not in this PR: deferring async rpc callbacks while `genro.src.building` would close the re-entry itself, but it changes the timing of every page whose `_T` strings are not cached; better in a change of its own.

## Tests

- New `gnrjs/tests/build_queue_nested_insert.test.js` (vm with the real `gnrbag`/`gnrdomsource`/`genro_src`, only the DOM creation stubbed): nested inserts queued during a build, a deeper insert under a queued ancestor, an update of a queued node, a failing build in the queue, `_isBuilding` after a failed build. All five fail on the previous code with the errors seen in the browser.
- `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 219/219.
- Browser, sandboxpg, `06_grouplet_navigation` in full: 10 loads, two of them through the re-entrant path; every load ends with `building` false and an empty queue, no console errors, Next builds the Shipping step on test_13 and test_14, the booking wizard of test_15 goes from Period to Holder in its dialog, the MultiButtons of test_2/3/9 keep and move their selection; a build made to fail on the page shows as `Uncaught Error` with its build stack, and the page keeps building.

items.title: fix: labledbox no longer wraps its content twice when rebuilt
items.body:
Fixes #1763

## Problem

With `groupletGrid(additem='phantom')` in cards layout and a `handler` template, the phantom card wrapped every lbl'd field twice (a `labledBox` nested inside the `labledBox_content` of another) when the grid sat in a form whose record arrived with stored rows.

## Root cause

`labledbox.onBuilding` (`gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_widgets.js`) restructures its source node in place: the children move into a label box and a content box. It ran again on every build of the same source node, so a rebuild nested a second label/content pair inside the first content box.

The grid triggers such a rebuild: the phantom is mounted as soon as the grid is built (empty store), then the form load replaces the store and `_fullSync` renders the rows under `bodyNode.freeze()` / `unfreeze()`. `unfreeze()` rebuilds the whole body, the already built phantom included. Regular tiles are built only once, which is why they were fine.

## Fix

`labledbox.onBuilding` returns early when the node already holds the label box it built (`_labelNode`'s parent is a child of the node). A rebuild now reuses the existing structure. The guard is in the widget, so any rebuild of a labled widget is covered, not only the grid's.

## Demo

`test_grouplet_grid/08_phantom_row.py` gets `test_08_phantom_cards_in_form`: phantom cards with a `formlet(cols='2fr 1fr')` handler inside a memory form loaded with one row.

## Verification

- Before the fix: the new case shows the phantom labels doubled (`Drug|Drug|Dose|Dose|...`, 5 nested wrappers).
- After: one label per field, same as the stored card; typing into the phantom promotes it and the next phantom is clean; a second form load keeps it clean.
- The other phantom/entry grids of the page (struct, cards, empty, fillParent, entry) are unchanged, no console errors.
- `gnrwdg/formlet`: calling `rebuild()` on a formlet keeps its 6 labels, no nested wrappers.
- flake8 clean; full test suite green in the pre-commit hook (3581 passed, 136 skipped).

items.title: [BUG] groupletGrid fillParent demo pages render empty
items.body:
### Problem Description

The testhandler pages `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/05_fill_parent` and `06_fill_parent_scenarios` render empty: the groupletGrid shows no tabs or cards, and the browser console fills with `unresolved relativepath .demo_nofill.chapters`, `.demo_fill.chapters`, `.vtabs.chapters`.

- The row seeds store `label` / `descr` as node attributes (`setItem(key, Bag(), label=...)`), while `titleField='label'` and `^.label` read the row values, so once anchored the tabs show "Untitled" and the cards are blank.

Expected: both panels of 05 (fillParent=False / True) and the three scenarios of 06 show titled tabs and filled cards.

### Reproduction Steps

1. `gnr web serve gnrdevelop -p 8082` (with `gnr web daemon` running)
2. Open http://localhost:8082/test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/05_fill_parent

develop, gnrdevelop instance (sqlite), Chromium

items.title: [BUG] Item memory store on a whole record rewrites it and loses change tracking
items.body:
## Problem Description

A `gnr.formstores.Item` memory store whose destination is a whole TH record (a GroupletForm with `locationpath='record'` inside a groupletPanel) misbehaves:

- `save_memory` rewrites every node of the destination: Bag values are popped and set again, so opening a group without edits marks the outer form changed (Bag columns, `__moved_related`).
- Unchanged scalars get their attributes replaced (`lazySet` with replace semantics), which drops the `_loadedValue` of fields edited earlier in another group: the outer form stops sending them on save and the edit is lost.
- `load_memory` keeps `*loaditem*` as the current pkey even when the destination record carries `_pkey`, so `relation=` handlers inside the form filter on `*loaditem*` and come up empty.

Expected: only changed values are written back, destination attributes are kept, and the loaded pkey is the destination record's.

## Reproduction Steps

1. thFormHandler on a table with a Bag column, `form.center.groupletPanel(value='^#FORM', ...)`, grouplets returning `locationpath='record'`.
2. Open a group, touch nothing: the outer form goes to `changed`.
3. Edit field A in group 1, then field B in group 2, save the outer form: A is not saved.
4. A grouplet mounting `dialogTableHandler(relation='@rows')`: the grid is empty for a record with rows.

## Environment

develop (26.09.x), any browser.

items.title: fix(gnrjs): the trigger index drops the subscriptions of discarded nodes and reports them
items.body:
## Problem

Any path that discards source content without going through `_trigger_upd` / `_trigger_del` leaves the `^attr` subscriptions of the discarded nodes in the trigger index. Today the leak surfaces as an unrelated `unresolved relativepath` from `absDatapath` at every event, or stays silent when the datapath is absolute and the lost node keeps updating a destroyed widget.

Two such paths were found in the five weeks after #1152 (#1301, cb12e187b0); the second was fixed by skipping silently, so nothing reports the next one.

## Change

`GnrTriggerIndex.publish` checks `isLostNode()` on each target. A lost one is not notified: one `console.error` names the tag, the attribute and the indexed path, and the subscription is removed from the index, so it is reported once and not at every event.

`isLostNode()` only follows parent pointers; `trigger_data` already does more work per target through `attrDatapath`/`absDatapath`. Not measured.

Out of scope: a matching guard in `_trigger_upd` for a node updated and then popped in the same build cycle (read from the code, not reproduced).

## Verification

- `trigger_index_frozen_discard.test.js`: a node discarded with `popNode(path, false)` is not notified, is reported once per subscription with its path, leaves the index, and a second publish logs nothing; a live subscription raises no error. The first is red without the change.
- `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 180 passed.
- Not verified in a browser.

Fixes #1300

items.title: [FEATURE] groupletWizard: per-step summary in the stepper and save on selected steps
items.body:
## Summary
groupletWizard: a per-step summary in the stepper, and a save on selected steps only.

## Problem or Need
- A wizard gives no recap of the choices made in previous steps: the user sees only the step captions.
- `saveOnNext` is all-or-nothing: `True` saves on every advance (a new record is inserted on the first step already), `False` saves only on complete, which dismisses the form. A wizard that must register the record when leaving one given step, then show it read-only on the last step, cannot be built.

## Proposed Solution
1. `stepSummary=True` (opt-in): under the caption of every COMPLETED step, render the `template` the step's grouplet declares in its `__info__()` (the same convention `groupletChunk` uses via `gr_getTemplatePars`), with `datasource=value`. Hidden on active and pending steps; a step without a template shows nothing. Vertical stepper: up to 2 lines with ellipsis; top stepper: one line, the step's width.
2. `saveOnNext` also accepts a step name, or a comma-separated list of step names (menu node labels): the advance saves only when leaving one of those steps. `True`/`False` keep their meaning.
3. `saveLabel`: the label of the Next button on a step that saves; default unchanged.
4. With `confirmedReadOnly=True`, the record saved by that step reopens on the last step, locked — also on a table without `draftField` (docstring updated accordingly).

## Impact and Scope
`gr_groupletWizard` / `gr_groupletWizardForm` in `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/`. Opt-in: existing wizards do not change. Requested for the teamset manual invoice wizard.

items.title: feat(grouplet): groupletGrid card mode gets formulas= and a totals= band
items.body:
Fixes #1439

## What

`groupletGrid` in card mode (`resource=` / `handler=`) gets, from Python, what
struct mode already had through its cells:

```python
pane.groupletGrid(storepath='.righe', handler=self.riga,
    formulas=dict(totale_riga='quantita*prezzo_unitario',
                  netto_riga='totale_riga/(1+aliquota_iva/100)'),
    totals=[dict(field='netto_riga', label='Net'),
            dict(name='iva', label='VAT', formula='totale_riga-netto_riga'),
            dict(field='totale_riga', label='Total', highlight=True)],
    totals_format='#,###.00', totals_hidden='^.vendita?=!#v')
```

- **`formulas=`** — per-row computed fields on the existing `GridChangeManager`
  formula columns. The fields an expression reads are put in the cellmap first
  (in card mode it starts empty), so editing a row recalculates the formula and
  a formula over another formula chains.
- **`totals=`** — each entry sums a row field (`setTotalizer`, stored at
  `<controllerPath>.totalize.<key>`, the namespace struct `totalize=True` uses)
  or is a `formula=` over the other totals, recomputed on `onUpdateTotalize`.
  `label`, `format`, `highlight` per entry.
- **The band** — one line of label/value pairs, right-aligned, grafted into a
  placeholder in the bottom slot (same mechanism as the struct footer).
  `totals_*` kwargs land on the placeholder, so `hidden` and dynamic params
  work; `totals_format` is the default format; `totals_sticky=True` pins the
  slot to the foot of the scrolling ancestor when the grid is not framed. In
  frame mode (`height` / `fillParent`) it stays put while the body scrolls.
- **Theme** — `--gg-totals-bg/-text/-highlight/-marker` on the container,
  reading the theme hooks `--totals-bg`, `--totals-text`, `--totals-highlight`,
  `--totals-marker`. Defaults: the strong surface (`--gg-header-bg`) and an
  accent rule under the highlighted figure — not the accent as text colour,
  which on several joanna variants (#8b1a6b, #4B0082) is unreadable on that
  surface.
- **Framed responsive cards** no longer stretch to the body's height
  (`align-content: start` on the responsive body): a framed grid is where
  the band naturally lives, and a single card filled it all.
- **`GridChangeManager.calculateFormula`** read `grid.structBag` unguarded; in
  card mode it is null, so `setFormula` could not work there. It now skips the
  `formula_*` dynamic params when there is no struct.

## Two traps met on the way

- A handler passed to `sourceNode.subscribe` must be a `function`, not an arrow:
  `funcApply` reads the signature off the source with
  `/function *\(([\w \,]*)\)/` and throws on `null[1]`.
- A `dataFormula` grafted into a live node after the page build starts listening
  after the first sums have been written, and `_onBuilt` does not fire there:
  hence the derived totals are computed by the controller.

## Tests

- Pre-commit: flake8 OK, `pytest` 2935 passed / 21 skipped.
- New page `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/07_card_totals` (testhandler),
  checked in the browser on a local instance running this branch:
  1. row formulas and band — edit qty 3→10: line 165,00, net 158,65, band
     226,17 / 14,93 / 241,10; delete a row and add a row, totals follow;
  2. `totals_hidden` toggles the band, flex layout kept;
  3. `height=`: rows scroll, band anchored;
  4. `totals_sticky` in a scrolling box: band pinned at the box foot;
  5. `--totals-*` set on an ancestor recolour the band;
  6. struct mode unchanged: formula column and aligned `totalize` footer.

First consumer, as a draft that waits for this: softwellsrl/cedi#14 — the DDT
wizard's Righe step, checked in the browser running this branch.

items.title: [BUG] updateRemoteContent re-entered before its in-flight lock: two fetches race and a stale content can be mounted last
items.body:
### Problem Description

A remote content node (`updateRemoteContent`, `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/gnrdomsource.js`) can end up showing content that no longer matches its attributes. On a `groupletWizard` the stepper and the wizard data (`step_index`, `current_resource`) are on one step while the DOM holds another step's grouplet, and it stays so until the next build.

Expected: whatever the order the server answers in, the content mounted last is the one fetched with the current attributes.

Root cause: `updateRemoteContent` takes its in-flight lock (`_remotebuilding`, gnrdomsource.js:1782) only right before the rpc, after code that can re-enter it:

1. `_T('Loading content')` (gnrdomsource.js:1777) makes a **synchronous** `getRemoteTranslation` call the first time a page translates the string (gnrlang.js:77).
2. In dojo 1.1 every XHR ends with `_watchInFlight()` (`dojo/_base/xhr.js:568`), which fires the handlers of every async request already completed but not yet polled (the poll runs every 50 ms, `_blockAsync` is never set).
3. So an async response that is in, e.g. the form's `loadRecordCluster`, is delivered **inside** the running `updateRemoteContent`. Its triggers change a remote attribute, `updateRemoteContent` is called again, finds `_remotebuilding` still unset and sends its own fetch. The outer call then resumes and sends the fetch it was preparing with the old attributes.
4. Two fetches are in flight on the same node; the one that lands last is mounted. The `_pendingRemoteUpdate` mechanism of b3ba5666ff never engages, because the second call saw no lock.

Live stack of the re-entered call: `updateRemoteContent:1777 → _T → genro.serverCall (sync) → dojo.xhrPost → _ioWatch → _watchInFlight → resHandle(loadRecordCluster) → form loaded → onLoaded controller → setRelativeData(current_resource) → updateRemoteContent`.

Exposed: every remote node with `_waitingMessage` whose dynamic attributes can change during the first sync `_T` of the page — `Grouplet` (hence `groupletWizard`, `groupletPanel`, `GroupletForm`) and `BagField` (genro_components.js:3124, which reloads on `#FORM.controller.loaded`).

### Reproduction Steps

1. A th form in a dialog whose content is a `groupletWizard` (`groupletWizardForm`) with `resumeStepField`, and a saved draft stored on step 2.
2. Reload the page, then open that draft (first dialog open of the page).
3. The wizard's grouplet node becomes visible and its `isVisibile` watch calls `updateRemoteContent()` while `current_resource` is still step 1; during its `_T` sync call the form load is delivered, `step_index` becomes 1 and the step-2 fetch starts nested.
4. Observed: two `remoteBuilder` rpcs in flight (step 2, then step 1). When step 2 answers first, the step-1 grouplet is mounted last: stepper on step 2, content of step 1.

The timing window is the 50 ms dojo poll, so it is intermittent. It becomes deterministic by calling the non-forced `updateRemoteContent()` from the `readystatechange` (readyState 4) of the form load XHR, i.e. when the response is in but not yet delivered, and delaying the step-1 response.

### If It Cannot Be Reproduced Externally

Observed on a client application's manual invoice wizard (`groupletWizardForm`, five steps, draft resume): first open after a reload showed step 1 on a draft stored on step 2; after a jump back to step 1, close and new record, step 1 in the stepper with step 2's tiles in the DOM. Both traced with instrumentation (rpc / merge / trigger log) to the double fetch described above.

### Environment

genropy develop (31584b4b4), dojo 1.1.1, Chrome, macOS.

items.title: groupletWizardForm: the first Next on a new record can leave the next step disabled
items.body:
## Problem

In `groupletWizardForm` with `saveOnNext`, the first Next on a new record can leave the next step with its fields disabled. The values typed in that step are lost, and the step comes back only after going Back and forward again.

The cause is a race between two calls that `gnr_grouplet.wizardStepForward` (`grouplet.js`) starts together:

1. `mainForm.lazySave()`. On a new record this is an insert, followed by a reload of the form with its real pkey.
2. `SET .step_index = idx + 1`, which builds the next step on the server and loads the step form.

The step form is a child of the main form. When the parent loads a pkey different from the one the child knows, the child is aborted (`genro_frm.js:222-227`). Going from `*newrecord*` to the saved pkey counts as a different record. After its own save the wizard deliberately does nothing (the `ownSave` branch of `on_loaded_js` in `grouplet.py`), so nobody reloads the step.

- **The reload lands first:** the abort hits a step form that is about to be reloaded by the new step. Nothing is visible.
- **The next step lands first:** the abort empties an already loaded step form (pkey `null`). Its status becomes `noItem` at the first change, and its fields are disabled.

Measured on a manual invoice wizard in teamset (softwellsrl/teamset#162): the next step was loaded at +345 ms and the insert reload arrived at +361 ms. It fails or passes run by run, depending on how heavy the insert is compared with the next step. CEDI's DDT and load wizards follow the same path. They have not shown it, most likely because their next steps are slower to build than their inserts.

## Fix

Advance only once the insert has landed. When the advance saves a new record, `wizardStepForward` records the target index instead of setting it. The reload that follows the wizard's own save (the `ownSave` branch) then moves to that step, so the step is built on the saved record.

Existing records do not change: `lazySave` does not reload them, so they advance immediately as today. If the insert fails, the wizard stays on the current step instead of moving on with an unsaved record.

items.title: [FEATURE] groupletGrid entry row: say which required field is missing on Enter
items.body:
## Summary

In a `groupletGrid` with `additem='entry'`, Enter (or the add button) with a `validate_notnull` field still empty refuses the row silently: the field gets the focus and nothing says why.

## Problem or Need

`_addEntry()` stops on `_entryMissingField()` and focuses that field, assuming "its own validation message shows on focus". It does not:

- the entry row is built with `parentForm:false`, so no form handler runs `validateFromDatasource` on its widgets, and a row built at page start also skips the build-time validation in `gnrdomsource.js` (`if (genro.src._started && this.widget)`). A field the user never typed in carries no validation error;
- even with one, the focus tooltip (`displayMessage`) is skipped for a blank value, so a `notnull` error would not show there anyway.

The cursor jumps to a field and the user has to guess the reason. Example: an invoice-rows grid whose VAT select is `validate_notnull` (test page `test/inputfields/filtering_data_null`, added by #1541).

## Proposed Solution

When `_addEntry()` finds a missing required field:

- validate it for `notnull` and set the result on the field, so it shows its error state while the row is being typed. The existing `:not(:focus-within)` rule in `grouplet.css` keeps the row muted once the focus leaves it;
- publish `floating_message` with "<field label>: Required field", the message a field outside a form already publishes on a user change (`_doChangeInData`);
- focus the field.

Clearing the entry row (Enter, Esc, record load) sets its data again, which resets the error, so the cleared row stays quiet as #1541 expects.

## Considered Alternatives

- CSS only: the entry row already mutes its fields until one is focused, but there is no error state to show, since nothing validates the row.
- Validating the whole row on mount: every required field would turn red as soon as the row gets the focus, before the user reaches it.

## Impact and Scope

Every `groupletGrid` with `additem='entry'` and required fields, struct or template rows. Only `grouplet_grid.js` changes.

## Additional Information

Not in scope:

- a "required" marker before Enter: `updateValidationClasses` sets `gnrrequired`, which has no CSS rule;
- the "New row" placeholder goes on the first required text-like field (`GroupletGridPhantomTile._mountBody`), in the example the VAT select rather than the description.

items.title: fix(form): a torn down widget no longer keeps the form invalid or changed
items.body:
Fixes #1476

## What

- `unregisterChild` forgets the node in `invalidFields` and `invalidDojo` (new `forgetInvalidChild`). A torn down widget, e.g. a deleted groupletGrid or includedView row with a required field left empty or a bad number, kept `isValid()` false until the next record load: `save()` answered `invalid` with the label of a widget that no longer existed.
- `triggerDEL` builds the changekey from the parent bag's path plus the node label. `Bag._pop` removes the node before emitting `del`, so `kw.node.getFullpath()` ended in `#-1`: the `isNewNode` entry of an added-then-deleted row was never popped, its children's entries stayed, and the form stayed `changed` after an add + delete.

## Verification

- `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 173 pass. The new `form_torn_down_field.test.js` fails on `develop` (4/4) and passes with the fix.
- Browser, `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/02_grid_db` on sandboxpg, regione LOM: add a province row, leave `nome` empty, delete the row, Salva. Before: "Campo non valido" with no field to fix. After: `invalidFields`, `invalidDojo` and `changesLogger` empty, form valid and unchanged.

items.title: [FEATURE] groupletGrid: phantom row, entry row and template rows with multi-selection
items.body:
## Summary

`groupletGrid` gets spreadsheet-like ways to enter rows, without the `+`/`-` buttons that sit badly in the struct (excel-like) layout.

## Phantom row — `additem='phantom'`

- A blank trailing row (or card) that stores nothing until a value is typed in it; the first value turns it into a real row and a new blank row appears.
- A row added this way and emptied again is dropped; loaded rows are not, and `minRows` / a locked form are respected.
- Visible on an empty grid too.

## Entry row — `additem='entry'`

- A row (or card) pinned above the rows, on its own band with a light shadow: Enter or the `↵` button appends its values at the tail, clears it and keeps the focus there.
- `keepable` fields keep their value for the next row: in struct mode the keeper is a pin in the column header (`keepable=True` on the cell), elsewhere the theme's keeper; `keepable='*'` always keeps. After Enter the focus goes to the first field not kept.
- Required fields (`validate_notnull`) stop the entry.

## Template rows — `rowTemplate`

- With `additem='entry'`, `rowTemplate` (or the grouplet's own `template`) makes the rows read-only one-line summaries; in struct mode they are the struct's cells rendered read-only.
- A click loads the row in the entry row, Enter saves it in place, Esc gives it up; the edited row's delete sits beside the save button.
- Cmd/Shift+click selects several rows; `rowCheckbox=True` adds a checkbox per row and a select-all one (struct header, or the selection bar), mail-list style.
- `selectionmenu` (same shape as `editmenu`) defines the actions on the selected rows, shown in a bar below the rows: `delete` is a preset button (the store's standard delete dialog), the other entries go in a kebab and run their `action` with `rowKeys` and `grid`.

## Paste

- Pasting tab/semicolon/comma separated text into a field of the phantom or entry row adds one row per line, mapping the columns from the field pasted into; a header line is skipped.

## Other

- The row delete is a light trash icon instead of the `×` (red on hover).
- `fillParent`: no outer scroll — header and footer stay put, only the body scrolls.

Test page: `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/08_phantom_row`.

items.title: [FEATURE] groupletGrid card mode: declarative formulas= and a totals= footer band
items.body:
## Summary

A totals footer for `groupletGrid` in card mode (`resource=` / `handler=`),
declared from Python: per-row `formulas=` and a one-line `totals=` band in the
bottom slot, styled through theme tokens.

## Problem or Need

In `struct=` mode a column with `totalize=` gets an aligned footer for free. In
card mode there is nothing: the engine is there (`GridChangeManager`, and the
controller's public `setTotalizer` / `setFormula`), but only from JS, and no
footer is drawn. Every application that needs a document total under a card
grid builds its own band by hand — a `dataController` walking the rows with
`digest`, three `div`s, its own colours, its own sticky positioning.

`setFormula` does not actually work in card mode either:
`GridChangeManager.calculateFormula` reads `grid.structBag.getItem('#0.#0')`,
and in card mode `structBag` is null. The formula's dependencies are also only
detected against fields already in the cellmap, which in card mode starts empty,
so a row edit never recalculates it.

## Proposed Solution

```python
pane.groupletGrid(storepath='.righe', resource='riga_ddt',
    formulas=dict(totale_riga='quantita*prezzo_unitario',
                  netto_riga='totale_riga/(1+aliquota_iva/100)'),
    totals=[dict(field='netto_riga', label='Netto'),
            dict(name='iva', label='IVA', formula='totale_riga-netto_riga'),
            dict(field='totale_riga', label='Totale', highlight=True)],
    totals_format='#,###.00',
    totals_hidden='==causale!="VENDITA"', totals_causale='^.causale')
```

- `formulas={field: expression}`: per-row computed fields, through the existing
  `GridChangeManager` formula columns. The fields an expression reads are
  registered as its triggers, so editing a row recalculates it.
- `totals=[...]`: each entry either sums a row field (`field=`, via
  `setTotalizer`, stored at `<controllerPath>.totalize.<field>`) or is a
  `formula=` over the other totals (stored under `name=`). `label`, `format`,
  `highlight` per entry.
- `totals_*` kwargs go to the band itself (`hidden`, dynamic params, `format`
  default, `sticky`).
- The band is drawn in the bottom slot as one line of label/value pairs,
  right-aligned. With `height`/`fillParent` the body scrolls and the band stays
  at the foot; `totals_sticky=True` pins it at the foot of the scrolling
  ancestor in the unframed layout.
- Colours through new tokens on `.grouplet_grid_container`, defaulting to the
  theme's strong surface and accent: `--gg-totals-bg` (`--gg-header-bg`),
  `--gg-totals-text` (`--gg-header-text`), `--gg-totals-highlight`
  (`--gg-accent`).
- `GridChangeManager.calculateFormula` tolerates a null `structBag` (no
  `formula_*` dynamic params in that case).

## Considered Alternatives

- Reusing the struct footer: it is laid out cell by cell under the columns,
  which card mode does not have.
- Leaving it to applications: that is what happens today, and each copy
  re-implements the same sum-of-products loop and chooses its own colours.

## Impact and Scope

Every card-mode `groupletGrid` that shows document rows (DDT, orders, loads,
budgets). Struct mode is untouched. A test page is added under
`test_grouplet_grid`.

## Additional Information

First consumer: the DDT wizard in softwellsrl/cedi, which today draws this band
by hand (`grouplets/ddt/righe.py`, `_footer_totali`).

items.title: [FEATURE] multiButton minimal option for the light text-button look
items.body:
### Summary
Give the light multiButton look (text buttons, selected one bold and underlined, no button chrome) a semantic option on the widget: `multiButton(..., minimal=True)`.

### Problem or Need
The light look only exists as descendant rules of the `mobile_bar` class in `gnrjs/gnr_d11/css/gnrbase_css/12_gnr_multibutton_misc.css`. A form that just wants a lighter multiButton has to wrap it in a `div(_class='mobile_bar')`, borrowing a class named after a mobile toolbar. Passing `_class` to the widget does not help: it replaces `multibutton_container` instead of adding to it.

### Proposed Solution
- `gnr.widgets.MultiButton` pops a `minimal` option and adds `multibutton_minimal` to the container class.
- The CSS rules of the light look are shared between `.mobile_bar` and `.multibutton_minimal`; the mobile-only rules (toolbar background, single-button hiding, portrait media query) stay on `mobile_bar`, which keeps working as before (grouplet panels, user preferences).

Any form or toolbar using a multiButton as a light switch (e.g. the Headline/Sidebar design switch of the html template editor). No change for existing `mobile_bar` users.

items.title: [BUG] groupletWizard: closing the dialog drops the current step's unsaved changes without asking
items.body:
## Problem Description

In a wizard run by `groupletWizardForm`, changes typed in the current step live in the step form (`<frameCode>_step_form`) until Back or Next saves them into the main record. The step form is not registered among the main form's `childForms`, so `GnrFrmHandler.load()` (`genro_frm.js`, the `childForms` loop before a dismiss) never sees it. When the main record is unchanged, e.g. right after a Next that saved it, closing the dialog dismisses at once and the step's changes are lost without any prompt.

## Reproduction Steps

1. `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplets/06_grouplet_navigation`, `test_11_wizard_resume`: add a ticket, fill Subject, press Next.
2. On Rows, add a row and type something in it.
3. Close the dialog: it closes without asking, and the row is gone when the ticket is reopened.

## Expected

Closing with unsaved step changes asks, like any other pending change (Discard / Cancel only, see #1496).

## Environment

genropy develop, any browser.

items.title: [BUG] MultiButton buttons still queued for build keep the previous selection
items.body:
### Problem Description

Follow-up of #1507 (#1508), raised in its review.

MultiButton `setValue` (`gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_components.js`) skips the buttons that have no `domNode` yet, i.e. still queued for build. `makeButtons` gives each button its selected class when it creates it, from the value of that moment. If the value changes again before the queued buttons are built — items reloaded and value set inside the same running build — the buttons are built with the previous selection: the value is the new one, the highlighted button the old one.

Expected: a button still queued for build is built with the selection of the current value.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Open `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplets/06_grouplet_navigation/3` (groupletPanel with a MultiButton).
2. Inside a running build (e.g. the `onCreated` of a node inserted in the page), reload the MultiButton items and then set its value to the second code.
3. The value is the second code, the first button is still the one marked `multibutton_selected`.

### Environment

genropy `develop` (1b2f864600), sandboxpg instance, Chrome.

items.title: fix(widgets): let dijit see a lightButton mousedown
items.body:
A click on a `lightButton` right after typing in a field acted on the value the field had **before** the edit.

## Root cause

`LightButton.created` (`gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_widgets.js`) stops mousedown propagation, so the mousedown never reaches `document`, where dijit hooks `dijit._onTouchNode` (`dijit/_base/focus.js:187`). That handler is what walks the ancestor chain and calls `_setStack`, which blurs the widget being left **synchronously** — and a dijit textbox only writes its value to the data bag from `_onBlur`.

With the mousedown swallowed, the only thing left is the native `blur`, whose handler `_onBlurNode` defers `_setStack([])` on a **100 ms timer** (`focus.js:231`). `_clickHandlerDo` is synchronous, so the click wins that race: the value is not in the bag yet and validation has not re-run.

Where it shows: a grouplet wizard. The first click on Next found the mandatory field still empty, `form.isValid()` refused, and nothing appeared to happen; a second click, more than 100 ms later, worked.

## Fix

Notify the focus manager explicitly before stopping propagation — exactly what the stop was taking away, with the stop itself left in place.

## Also in this PR

- `wizardNext` reports invalidity on the form's own message channel instead of publishing to `_gnrRoot`: a wizard normally lives in a dialog, where a `_gnrRoot` message lands behind it, and `_buildInvalidMessage()` names the offending fields.
- `groupletGrid` focuses the first editor of a row added through the action bus, so `+ Add row` lands the caret in the new row.

## Verification

JS only, no test harness: checked at source level and to be exercised in the browser on a grouplet wizard (fields + righe grid) and on a plain form with lightButtons next to edited fields.

items.title: feat(adm): hosting preference keys read-only in the workspace preference page
items.body:
## Summary
Follow-up of #1672 (issue #1663): in a multidomain workspace, the preference keys set by the hosting layer (`storetable.preferences`) are shown with their effective value and are read-only in the workspace's own preference page, for every pane (framework, erpy, applications) without per-pane code.

Stacked on `feature/multidomain-hosting-preferences` (#1672): it uses `multidb.getHostingPreference`. Retarget to `develop` once #1672 is merged.

## Design
**Why not `_protect_write` / `protected_by_*`.** That mechanism is "whole record read-only, with exceptions": any `_protect_write` puts the form in `status='readOnly'`, which suppresses the save, and widgets without an explicit exemption are locked. Here the opposite is needed: a few paths locked, the rest editable and savable. Data-node attributes cannot carry the mark either: the GroupletForm memory store resets the node attributes in `load_memory`.

**Client (`genro_frm.js`), generic.**
- A loaded record can carry `_protected_paths`: record-relative paths, comma separated.
- `form.getProtectedPaths()` returns them as absolute datapaths. A form with an Item store (`store.locationpath`, e.g. GroupletForm) also inherits the parent form's protected paths below its `locationpath`, mapped onto its own record. Legacy `prefpane_<pkg>` panes and `app_preferences` grouplets are covered with no change.
- `applyDisabledStatus` disables a registered widget whose `value` path is, or lies under, a protected path.

**Server (`adm.preference`, wired by `ph_appPreferencesForm` as store load/save handlers).**
- Load, `applyHostingPreferences`: on `_mainpref_`, in a workspace (multidomain, not the rootstore), writes the hosting leaves into the loaded `data` and sets `_protected_paths`.
- Save, `restoreTenantPreferences`: `data` has `_sendback=True`, so the whole Bag comes back. On every hosting path it puts back the tenant's own value (or removes the key if the tenant had none). Without this, the provider values shown in the form would be copied into the tenant's `_mainpref_`.

**Why form handlers and not a table trigger.** An `onUpdating` trigger would also block `setPreference` from scripts, including the application migrations that clear the tenant copy of a hosting key. Load and save stay symmetric in the form.

## Checks
- [x] flake8 on the touched Python files: clean. `node --check` on `genro_frm.js`: OK.
- [x] Full suite on this branch: 3235 passed, 21 skipped.
- [x] Against local `icond2_apps` (worktree code through `GENRO_GNRFOLDER`), workspace `rossi`:
  - Server side: `_protected_paths` set, the form shows the hosting value, and `restoreTenantPreferences` puts back the tenant value.
  - Page `/rossi/adm/app_preference`, Erpy Core pane, with a test hosting key `er_core.dati_sociali.anagrafica_id` (removed afterwards): the field shows the hosting value and is disabled, while the other fields stay editable.
  - Saving a change to a tenant field (`comuni_istat`) writes it, and `anagrafica_id`, `owner_name` and `default_studio_id` in the tenant's `_mainpref_` keep the tenant values.
- [ ] No automated multidomain test: the framework test suite has no multidb/multidomain instance.

## Notes
- `Bag.getLeaves()` returns the folder nodes below the first level: the recursion in `_deepIndex` does not pass `excludeFolders`. It is filtered locally here; the core fix is left for a separate change because it also changes `separateCols` in `gnrsqldata/query.py`.
- Saving from the page opened standalone (outside the frame index) shows a client error `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'refresh')`, raised by the `gnr.serverEvent.refreshNode` change sent by `adm.preference.trigger_onUpdated`. This PR does not touch that code. Not verified on the base branch.

items.title: Form keeps invalid fields and change entries of torn down widgets
items.body:
## Symptom

A row widget of a form (a groupletGrid row, an includedView row, any remote-rebuilt subtree) that holds an invalid value is torn down, e.g. the row is deleted. From then on the form cannot be saved: `save()` answers `invalid`, the message names a label of a widget that no longer exists (`TextBox_1: Invalid value`) and `focusFirstInvalidField` has nothing to focus. Only a record reload clears it.

Reproduced on `test/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/02_grid_db` (regione LOM): add a province row, leave the required `nome` empty, delete the row with its `×`, then Salva.

## Cause

`updateInvalidField` and `dojoValidation` record the widget in `invalidFields` (keyed by data path, values are sourceNode ids) and `invalidDojo` (keyed by sourceNode id). When the widget is torn down, `unregisterChild` only drops it from `_register`: the two collections keep the entry, and `isValid()` reads them. `checkInvalidFields` would prune the dead ids, but it runs only for remote dynamic forms.

A second bookkeeping leak comes with every `popNode` inside the form data: `Bag._pop` removes the node from `_nodes` before it emits the `del` trigger, so in `triggerDEL` the changekey built from `kw.node.getFullpath()` ends in `#-1`. The `isNewNode` entry of a row added and then deleted is never popped, nor are its children's entries, and the form stays `changed` after an add + delete.

## Fix

- `unregisterChild` forgets the node in `invalidFields` and `invalidDojo`.
- `triggerDEL` builds the changekey from the parent bag's path and the node label.
- Regression tests in `gnrjs/tests/`.

items.title: fix(gnrjs): take the remote content lock before anything that can re-enter
items.body:
Fixes #1436

## Problem

`updateRemoteContent` (`gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/gnrdomsource.js`) took its in-flight lock `_remotebuilding` only right before the rpc. On the way there `_T('Loading content')` makes, the first time a page translates it, a **sync** `getRemoteTranslation` call, and in dojo 1.1 every XHR runs `_watchInFlight()`, which delivers the async responses already in. A form load delivered there changes a remote attribute and calls `updateRemoteContent` again: it finds no lock, sends its own fetch, then the outer call sends the one it was preparing with the old attributes. Two fetches race on the same node, the last to land is mounted, and the `_pendingRemoteUpdate` re-fetch of b3ba5666ff never engages.

Seen on a `groupletWizard` (first open of a draft after a reload): stepper and wizard data on step 2, DOM holding step 1. The same exposure applies to every remote node with `_waitingMessage` (`Grouplet`, `BagField`).

## Change

- `_remotebuilding` is taken right after the in-flight check, before `evaluateOnNode` and `_T`: a re-entering call now sets `_pendingRemoteUpdate` like any trigger arriving mid-flight.
- `_releaseRemoteUpdate(async)` releases the lock and runs the pending re-fetch; it is used by every exit (cached attributes, false `_if`, rpc landing).

The mid-flight semantics of b3ba5666ff are unchanged: a result that lands with an update pending is still mounted, then replaced by the re-fetch.

## Verification

- `gnrjs/tests/remote_content_reentry.test.js`: re-entry from `_T` leaves a single fetch in flight and the re-entered attributes mounted last; the mid-flight re-fetch and the `_if` release keep working. Without the fix the two re-entry tests fail (fetches `['second', 'first']`, `first` mounted last).
- `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 104 pass, 0 fail.
- Live, on the wizard where it was observed, with the change injected in the page: the instrumented deterministic repro (form load delivered inside the sync `_T`, step-1 answer delayed) ends on step 2; before the change it ends on step 1 under a step-2 stepper. Jumping back while a fetch is in flight also settles on the current step.

items.title: Trigger index: drop subscriptions of lost nodes with a visible error
items.body:
## Context

#1152 replaced the global sweep of `refreshSourceIndexAndSubscribers` with an incremental cleanup of the trigger index in `_trigger_upd` / `_trigger_del`. Any path that discards source content without going through those two handlers leaves the `^attr` subscriptions of the discarded nodes in the trie. The first such path found is content discarded under a frozen node (batch monitor, timesheet_viewer, grouplet_grid), fixed in the linked PR at the source.

## Proposal

`GnrTriggerIndex.publish` reaches every subscription registered on the event path, its ancestors and its subtree. A subscription whose node no longer belongs to the live source tree (`isLostNode()`) is a leak by definition: the node was discarded without cleanup.

Rather than silently skipping it, `publish` could:

- log a `console.error` naming the node (tag, attribute, last known datapath) so the leaking discard path is visible and gets fixed at the source;
- remove the subscription from the index, so the error is reported once per leaked subscription and not at every event.

The point is not to hide the leak: today it surfaces as an unrelated `unresolved relativepath` from `absDatapath` on every event, which points at the symptom rather than at the discard that caused it. A dedicated message would point at the cause.

## Out of scope

The frozen-node discard itself, fixed by the linked PR.

items.title: [BUG] GroupletForm loadOnBuilt: entering a wizard step asks about pending changes the build itself made
items.body:
## Problem Description

A `GroupletForm` built with `loadOnBuilt=True` (every `groupletWizard` / `groupletWizardForm` step) loads its record only after the step content is built: the load is queued in the grouplet's `_onRemote` (`gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_components.js:1066`, `this.form.load();`).

Anything the step writes into its own record during the build (`dataController(..., _onBuilt=True)`, a `dataRpc` `_else` branch, a result landing before the load) marks the step form as changed. The load that follows then finds a changed form and a `destPkey` (`*loaditem*`) different from the current pkey, and `load_store` opens the pending-changes dialog ("Modifiche pendenti in <frameCode>_step_form — Il record corrente è stato modificato") on the user's plain advance to the next step.

Those changes are not the user's: the load overwrites them anyway, and the step's triggers run again on the loaded record.

**Expected:** entering a step never asks about pending changes; the first load after the build discards the changes made by the build itself.

## Reproduction Steps

1. `groupletWizardForm` on a th form; in step 2 a `dataController(..., _onBuilt=True)` that SETs a field of the record (e.g. auto-select the only allowed value when the field is empty).
2. Open an existing record whose field is empty, advance from step 1 to step 2.
3. The pending-changes dialog appears. "Annulla modifiche" lets the load proceed and the step works.

Seen in a client project (booking wizard, page 2 auto-selects the only allowed service). A runtime patch passing `{discardChanges: true}` to that post-build load removes the dialog and the step fills correctly; both traced loads (step 1 and step 2) had the form already changed.

## Proposed fix

In `GroupletForm.createContent`, the `loadOnBuilt` load discards pre-load changes: `this.form.load({discardChanges:true});` (and the same for the `startKey` load). Changes made by the user after the load are unaffected.

## Environment

GenroPy `develop` @ 0c5ef6dd05, macOS, Chrome-based browser pane.
