[TASK] groupletGrid: introduce GroupletDataStore (model façade)

labels.name: task
labels.description: Technical task, maintenance, or internal improvement

items.body:
## Summary

Introduce a `gnr.GroupletDataStore` class as the model-side façade of the groupletGrid widget. Three modes (`internal` / `proxy` / `adapter`) so the same controller works against an internal Bag or against an external store (BagStore / ValuesBagRows / AttributesBagRows / Selection / RpcBase).

Full design document already in the worktree: `docs/groupletgrid_store_integration.html` (43k, post Item 12/13).

## Objective

Today the controller mixes Model + View. Every data access goes through `this.storebag()` and `bag.getNodes()` directly, with `popNode`/`setItem` mutations scattered. This forecloses three things:

1. **Filter/sort layer** — every Grid has a `view-transform layer` between data and display (`createFiltered` populates `_filtered`, `attributes_mixin_get` is the rendering hook). Our widget will need the same when multi-select + bulk delete + grouping come.
2. **Adoption of external stores** — siblings emit a `BagStore` (`ValuesBagRows`) or `dataSelection` (`AttributesBagRows`/`Selection`/`RpcBase`); today the widget can't consume those without duplication.
3. **Status / lock / hasChanges propagation** — formStore-backed widgets export `hasChanges()`, `hasErrors()`, `setLocked()`. The widget today can't surface these.

The phased rollout (see design doc § 7) lets us land the class incrementally without breaking test_1-12: phase 1 is internal-only, all proxy/adapter API stubbed with `console.warn` returning sensible defaults.

## Scope

### Phase 1 (this issue, scope minimum)

In scope:

- Create class `gnr.GroupletDataStore` in a new file `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet_data_store.js` (or inline at the bottom of `grouplet_grid.js` if simpler — TBD during implementation).
- Mode `internal` only. Public API surface complete; non-internal methods stub-warn.
- Controller constructs `this.dataStore = new gnr.GroupletDataStore(this, 'internal')` on init.
- Migrate the existing scattered `bag.getNodes()` / `popNode` / `setItem` callsites to go through `this.dataStore.<method>()`. Six migration steps detailed in design doc § 7.
- Tests 1-12 unchanged.

Out of scope:

- Mode `proxy` (BagStore siblings).
- Mode `adapter` (AttributesBagRows / Selection / RpcBase).
- Filter / sort UI.
- Lock propagation.
- `hasChanges()` / `hasErrors()` real implementation.
- BagStore siblings emit on the Python side.

### Phase 2 (follow-up issue, not this one)

- Mode `proxy` for ValuesBagRows pass-through.
- Add the `store_*` kwarg prefix on `gr_groupletGrid` (mirroring `bagGrid`).
- `linkedGrids` integration, lock propagation.

### Phase 3 (follow-up issue)

- Mode `adapter` for AttributesBagRows / Selection / RpcBase with materialization cache.

## Technical Details / Notes

Design doc location: `docs/groupletgrid_store_integration.html` in the worktree. Read it before starting. Covers:

- §2: architecture, three modes, when to use each.
- §3: matrix of every API the Grid uses on the store (Steal / Delegate / Adapt / Stub / Skip).
- §3bis: API of the Grid widget itself (filter/sort orchestration, render-lifecycle, selection-keeper, mutation-orchestration).
- §4: where the groupletGrid controller touches `bag` today (file:line) — these are the migration points.
- §5: full GroupletDataStore public API.
- §6: dispatch table per mode.
- §7: 6-step phase 1 plan.
- §8: 9 known risks + mitigations.
- §9: 6 open questions.

Key insight from the doc (§3bis callout): `attributes_mixin_get` is the architectural proof that **there is always a filter/sort layer between data and display** in a Grid, even when no filter UI is active. Our widget today bypasses this; the refactor introduces `dataStore.visualOrder()` as the equivalent — internal `_filtered` + `sortedBy` apply transparently, no-op when empty.

Phase 1 stub pattern (from doc §7):

```js
hasChanges() {
    console.warn('[GroupletDataStore] hasChanges() not implemented '
                 + 'in internal mode (requires external store)');
    return false;
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Class `gnr.GroupletDataStore` defined with full public API surface.
- [ ] Mode `internal` implemented; mode `proxy` / `adapter` stub-warn.
- [ ] Controller delegates all bag access to `this.dataStore.<method>()`.
- [ ] No direct `bag.getNodes()`, `bag.popNode()`, `bag.setItem(_position)` calls in the controller (except inside `_doMoveTile*` which becomes the data store's `moveItem`).
- [ ] All 12 test pages (`11_grouplet_grid.py` test_1-9, `12_grouplet_grid_db.py`, budget_editor) visually unchanged.
- [ ] `_askAndDeleteItem` delegates to `dataStore.deleteItemAsk(pkey)`.

## Dependencies

- None blocking. The Tile class refactor (commits on `feat-grouplet-grid`) is complete; the dataStore is the next architectural step.
- Related: #898 (DnD migration) is independent and can land before, after, or in parallel.

items.title: [TASK] groupletGrid: migrate DnD to genro.dom.* helpers + dedup wire methods

labels.name: task
labels.description: Technical task, maintenance, or internal improvement

items.body:
## Summary

Rewrite the groupletGrid drag-and-drop using the declarative DnD attributes supported by `baseHtml` widgets (i.e. any `<div>`-backed sourceNode). Today the widget reimplements ~280 lines of HTML5 DnD wiring from scratch, when genropy already provides a clean attribute-based pipeline. **No widget tag change required** — the existing `<div>` tile wrapper supports the full DnD machinery via kwargs.

## Objective

Replace ~280 lines of manual `addEventListener` wiring + manual `setData/getData` + manual valid/foreign detection with declarative kwargs on the sourceNode, leveraging:

- `draggable: true` on the tile sourceNode → framework registers dragstart globally.
- `dragValue` / `onDrag_<type>` → payload composition; framework serialises via `setInDataTransfer`.
- `dropTarget: true`, `dropTypes: 'gg-tile-<dragCode>'` → declarative drop acceptance.
- `onDrop_gg_tile_xxx` callback → dispatch the `move` action on the action bus.
- `dragInfo.dragImageNode` populated in a hook for the struct-mode custom drag clone.
- Outline classes `canBeDropped` / `cannotBeDropped` added/removed automatically by `genro.dom.outlineShape` on `dropInfo.outline` — restyle via CSS to keep the current `gg-drop-target` / `gg-drop-target-invalid` look.
- `bag.moveNode(fromIdx, toIdx)` instead of `popNode + setItem(_position)` (one-line mirror of `gnr.Grid.mixin_moveRow`, genro_grid.js:2146).

## Scope

In scope:

- `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet_grid.js`:
  - Remove `_wireTileDnD` (184 lines), `_wireTabDnD` (130 lines), `_unwireTileDnD`, `_unwireTabDnD`, `_dragHandlesByPkey` storage.
  - Tile (`_mountWrapper`) and tab chip (`_addTabChip`) declare DnD via kwargs on the sourceNode (`draggable`, `dropTarget`, `dropTypes`, `onDrag_<key>`, `onDrop_<key>`).
  - Container drop area (`_wireContainerDnD`) follows the same pattern.
  - `_doMoveTile` reduced to `bag.moveNode(fromIdx, toIdx)`.
  - Replace `_setDragOver` / `_clearDragOver` / `_dragOverRow` with CSS styling of the `canBeDropped` / `cannotBeDropped` classes that the framework manages on `dropInfo.outline`.
- `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.css`:
  - Map current `.gg-drop-target` rules to `.canBeDropped` (or vice versa), and `.gg-drop-target-invalid` to `.cannotBeDropped` — whichever is less intrusive.

Out of scope:

- Public widget API changes — `dragCode` kwarg semantics preserved (isolated grids share a `dropTypes` token).
- Changing the tile wrapper tag (still `<div>` — declarative DnD works on any `baseHtml` sourceNode).
- Refactoring container DnD (only adapts the kwargs; the container is still a generic drop area).

## Technical Details / Notes

Reference reading (verified):

- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_widgets.js:158-310` — `baseHtml._creatingMain` extracts and wires `dropTarget`, `dropTargetCb`, `dropTargetCb_extra`, `onDrop_*`, `dragValue`, `draggable`.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_widgets.js:473-496` — `baseHtml.onDragStart` default returns `{'text/plain': dragValue}`; `baseHtml.fillDropInfo` sets `dropInfo.outline = dropInfo.domnode`.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_dom.js:1014-1057` — `getDragDropInfo` resolves the handler via `domnode.gnr`, sets `info.dragSourceInfo` for cross-instance routing.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_dom.js:1066-1106` — `onDragOver` calls `canBeDropped`, applies `effectAllowed`/`dropEffect`, and toggles `canBeDropped` / `cannotBeDropped` classes on `dropInfo.outline` via `outlineShape`.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_dom.js:1198-1226` — `onDrop_standard` walks `dataTransferTypes`, dispatches to `inherited['onDrop_<typecode>']` callbacks declared on the sourceNode.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_dom.js:1261-1305` — `onDragStart` calls `handler.onDragStart` then any `onDrag_<key>` callback to compose `dragValues`, then `setInDataTransfer` serialises each into `dataTransfer`.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_grid.js:2291-2302` — drag image idiom (`auxDragImage` clone) we'll reuse identically for struct-mode tiles.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/gnrbag.js:1364` — `bag.moveNode(fromPos, toPos, doTrigger)` primitive.
- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_components.js:6111` — example of declarative `onDrop_trashable` callback in a real widget.

Payload contract (preserved for cross-grid kanban):

```js
// Declarative on the tile sourceNode:
{
    draggable: true,
    dropTarget: true,
    dropTypes: 'gg-tile-' + dragCode,
    onDrag_gg_tile_xxx: function(dragValues, dragInfo) {
        dragValues['gg-tile-' + dragCode] = {rowKey: pkey, nodeId: ctrl.nodeId};
    },
    onDrop_gg_tile_xxx: function(dropInfo, data) {
        genro.publish(ctrl.actionTopic, {
            action: 'move',
            rowKey: data.rowKey,
            sourceNodeId: data.nodeId,
            position: '<' + pkey
        });
    }
}
```

For the struct-mode drag image: hook into `onDrag_*` to populate `dragInfo.dragImageNode` with the cloned tile DOM (mirror genro_grid.js:2291-2302).

Regression risk areas:

- test_6 kanban DnD (cross-grid moves with shared `dragCode`).
- test_7 nested team (nested groupletGrids — must NOT have the inner DnD bubble up to outer).
- test_8 tabs (chip-level DnD).
- test_9 struct invoice (custom drag-image with `--gg-struct-columns`).
- budget_editor (struct + tabs combo).

The nested-grid isolation concern: the framework's `getEventInfo` walks up the DOM from `event.target` to the closest `sourceNode`. For nested groupletGrids the inner tile is itself a sourceNode, so the resolver picks it correctly — no manual `closest()` filter needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_wireTileDnD`, `_wireTabDnD`, `_unwireTileDnD`, `_unwireTabDnD`, `_dragHandlesByPkey`, `_setDragOver`, `_clearDragOver`, `_dragOverRow` removed.
- [ ] DnD declared via kwargs on tile sourceNode and tab chip sourceNode (chip is plain DOM today — may need to become a sourceNode `_('div', ...)` instead of `document.createElement('div')` to participate in the framework DnD).
- [ ] `bag.moveNode` used in `_doMoveTile`.
- [ ] All gallery test pages visually unchanged.
- [ ] Cross-grid kanban DnD continues to work end-to-end.
- [ ] Nested grouplet grids (test_7) keep correct drag isolation.
- [ ] Total DnD code reduced by ~200 lines.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Pre-refactor (rename, Tile class, dispatch unify) landed in `feat-grouplet-grid` on commits `d4e3db89`, `b2896809`, `d4eb136e`, `bbf4fc12`, `9f1bafba`.

## Note on prior misunderstanding

An earlier version of this issue described the migration as requiring a custom widget handler registration (à la `gnr.widgets.Grid`) and a tag change away from `<div>`. That was wrong: the declarative DnD attributes work on any `baseHtml`-backed sourceNode (`<div>`, `<span>`, etc.) without any handler subclassing. The only true requirement is that the tile wrapper is a sourceNode (`pane._('div', label, kw)`), which it already is.

items.title: fix(web): bagField without resource no longer raises UnboundLocalError
items.body:
## Problem

`bagField` without a `resource=` argument raises `UnboundLocalError` on the server. This is the common case: the client (`gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_components.js:3116-3118`) only sets `remote__if='resource'` when `resource` is actually present, so a resource-less `bagField` fires the remote unconditionally and 500s.

## Root cause

`gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwebpage.py` — `bagFieldDispatcher`:

```python
if resource:
    ...
    if table:
        mixinedClass = self.mixinTableResource(...)
    else:
        mixinedClass = self.mixinComponent(resource)
bagfieldmodule = getattr(mixinedClass,'__top_mixined_module',None)
```

`mixinedClass` is bound only inside `if resource:` (both arms of the inner `if table:` bind it), and read unconditionally right below — `UnboundLocalError` whenever `resource` is falsy. Regression from `0f81ea889` ("bagEditor with sourcecode", 2020-03-09), which introduced `mixinedClass`/`bagfieldmodule` without ever gating the read.

`bagfieldmodule` has **zero consumers** in the codebase today (it appears in exactly this one file, at the producer line and the `contentPane(...)` call). Its one former consumer was already dead before `0f81ea889` landed and was removed later. `None` is already a live, tolerated value: `mixinComponent(safeMode=True)` (`gnrwebpage.py:791-802`) swallows `GnrMixinNotFound` and returns `None`, so a `table=` bagField with a missing resource already produces `bagfieldmodule=None` in production today with no ill effect.

### Corrections to the issue's premise

- **Wrong test page path.** The test page lives at `projects/gnrcore/packages/test15/webpages/components/bagfieldpages/bagfield_test.py` — package `test15`, not `test`. URL: `/test15/components/bagfieldpages/bagfield_test`.
- **All four cases fail, not just one.** The page has `test_1_pane` (`method=`), `test_2_field`, `test_3_field` (`field=` override) and `test_4_resource` (which, despite its name, calls plain `fb.bagField('^.gamma')` / `fb.bagField('^.delta')` — no `resource=` at all). None of the four passes `resource=`, so all four take the falsy-`resource` branch and all four hit the `UnboundLocalError`. The issue's own evidence agrees: 7 failed requests = 1 + 2 + 2 + 2, i.e. every `bagField` on the page.
- **`method=` needs a second, independent fix** (see below) — otherwise `test_1_pane` still 500s after the `UnboundLocalError` fix, with `AttributeError: 'GnrCustomWebPage' object has no attribute 'bf_value'`.
- **`test_4_resource` stays broken by design**, for a separate reason unrelated to this bug (see "Out of scope" below).

## Change

**Hunk 1** — `gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwebpage.py`: seed `bagfieldmodule = None` before the `if resource:` branch and move the `getattr(...)` read inside it, so the `safeMode` → `None` case keeps flowing through the existing default and the method never holds a name that is unconditionally read but conditionally bound.

**Hunk 2** — `gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwebstruct/base.py:838-839`: `bagField(method=...)` wrote the attribute as `methodname`, but the JS pops `bfhandler` (`genro_components.js:3108`) — nothing maps one to the other, so the server always saw `bfhandler=None` and fell through to `bf_<field>`. Rename regression from `78f52f96d` ("bagfields update", 2020-02-27), which renamed the server-side parameter `methodname`→`bfhandler` and updated the JS but missed this call site. This aligns `bagField` with the adjacent `grouplet(handler=...)`, whose JS widget pops the matching name (`genro_components.js:3143`).

Both hunks ship together: hunk 1 alone still leaves `method=` silently broken, and the issue cannot be honestly closed without both — see "Open decisions" below for the alternative considered.

## Verification

- **New test**, real code path, no mocks of the fix itself: `gnrpy/tests/web/gnrwebpage_test.py::test_bagFieldDispatcher_without_resource_does_not_raise`. Calls `GnrWebPage.bagFieldDispatcher` directly with `resource=None` and a stub `bf_value` handler, asserts it returns without `UnboundLocalError` and that the pane receives `bagfieldmodule=None`.
  - Confirmed this test **fails on unmodified `develop`** with exactly the predicted `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'mixinedClass' where it is not associated with a value`, and passes after the fix.
- `flake8` on the three touched files: 0 errors. CI selection `flake8 . --count --select=F401,E9,F63,F7,F82 --show-source --statistics` on the whole tree: 0.
- Full suite: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/sql` → 841 passed, 59 skipped, 0 failed. The pre-commit hook additionally ran the complete suite including `tests/sql` → 2012 passed, 69 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Manual live check stayed manual — not performed in this environment.** Steps for a maintainer to confirm: start instance `gnrdevelop` (`projects/gnrcore/instances/gnrdevelop`, mounts `gnrcore:test15`), open `/test15/components/bagfieldpages/bagfield_test`, watch the network panel (the page GET itself is 200 either way). Expected: the 7 failing `bagField` POSTs on `develop` drop to 2 after both hunks (`test_4_resource`'s two fields, blocked by the separate defect below); with hunk 1 alone, 1 more than that.

## Related issue

Fixes #1101

## Out of scope — reported, not fixed here

`test_4_resource` relies on an implicit `bf_<pagename>` resource convention that `78f52f96d` deleted. Passing `resource=` sets `handlername='bf_main'` unconditionally, but every `BagFieldForm` subclass in the repo implements `bf_content`, not `bf_main` (`BagFieldForm` itself is `pass`). So the resource path the issue assumes works is *also* broken — including its one real-world caller in the `dform` package (`projects/gnrcore/packages/dform/resources/tables/dform_data/th_dform_data.py`). This is a separate, pre-existing defect independent of the `UnboundLocalError` fixed here; not addressed in this PR and no issue opened for it — flagging it here for a maintainer to decide whether it needs its own ticket.

## Open decisions

@dgpaci, three calls made while fixing this — flagging in case you'd have gone the other way:

1. **Ship the `method=`/`bfhandler` fix (hunk 2) together with the `UnboundLocalError` fix, rather than splitting it into its own PR.** Taken: together, since it closes the issue's `test_1_pane` case for real; the cost is one extra file and a second failure mode to re-verify in this same change. Splitting would keep a one-line diff but leave `method=` silently broken until someone files the follow-up.
2. **No guard added for a missing handler method** (e.g. `if not hasattr(self,handlername): raise ...`, mirroring `grouplet.py:21-23`, which would turn `test_4_resource`'s bare `AttributeError` 500 into a legible error message). Taken: skip, to keep the diff minimal — but it's worth doing separately, since it would make the residual `test_4_resource` breakage self-documenting instead of a raw 500.
3. **`bagField` is repaired rather than deprecated**, even though it's already labelled `//legacy: use grouplets instead of BagField` in the JS. Taken: repair, since deprecating outright would leave a live `UnboundLocalError` in `develop` and force `dform` to migrate first.

items.title: [BUG] groupletWizard step save crashes: relation nodes lost in the step form's record copy
items.body:
## Problem Description

Saving the step form of a `groupletWizard` bound to a table that has relations raises a 500:

```
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable
```

Every relation node of the record — plain foreign keys included — is routed to the
`relatedMany` branch of `writeRecordCluster` with a `None` cluster, and the loop
dereferences it.

**Expected**: the step save persists the main record's own columns; a relation node
with no content is skipped.

**Actual**: the first relation node encountered raises, so the wizard cannot advance
past its first step and no record is ever written.

## Reproduction Steps

1. A table with at least one FK and one one-to-many relation. In my case
   `cedi_vend.spedizione`: FKs `cliente_id`, `deposito_origine_codice`,
   `deposito_destinazione_codice`, `operazione_id`, plus the `@righe` many relation
   to `cedi_vend.spedizione_riga`.
2. A form-only webpage:
   ```python
   pane.thFormHandler(table='cedi_vend.spedizione', formId='spedizione',
                      formResource='FormRifornimento',
                      datapath='main.spedizione',
                      startKey='*newrecord*', autoSave=500)
   ```
3. The form resource mounts the wizard:
   ```python
   class FormRifornimento(Form):
       py_requires = 'gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet:GroupletHandler'

       def th_form(self, form):
           form.center.contentPane().groupletWizard(
               table='cedi_vend.spedizione', value='^#FORM.record',
               topic='rifornimento', frameCode='ddt_rifornimento_wizard',
               completeLabel='Close', saveMainFormOnComplete=True)

       def th_options(self):
           return dict(dialog_windowRatio=0.85, showtoolbar=False)
   ```
4. Step files under `resources/tables/spedizione/grouplets/rifornimento/`, step 1
   carrying the `validate_notnull` fields (two FK pickers).
5. Open the page, fill step 1's mandatory fields, press Next. `wizardNext` validates
   and saves the step form → 500.

## Traceback

```
File "gnr/web/_gnrbasewebpage.py", line 510, in saveRecordCluster
    record = tblobj.writeRecordCluster(recordCluster, recordClusterAttr)
File "gnr/sql/gnrsqltable/crud.py", line 621, in writeRecordCluster
    for sub_recordClusterNode in rel_recordCluster:
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable
```

## Analysis

`_splitRecordCluster` (crud.py:651-656) classifies every node whose label starts with
`@` by trusting a single attribute:

```python
if n.label.startswith('@'):
    if n.getAttr('mode') == 'O':
        relatedOne[n.label[1:]] = nodes.pop(j)
    else:
        relatedMany[n.label] = nodes.pop(j)
```

There is no model lookup, so a relation node that has lost its `mode` attribute is
indistinguishable from a many relation.

The cluster the step form submits is the `GroupletForm` memory-store copy of the main
form's record. In that copy every relation node has lost **both** `mode` and its
value. Measured live in the browser on the same record, comparing the main form's
record with the step form's copy:

| node | main form record | step form copy |
|---|---|---|
| `@cliente_id` | `mode='O'`, Bag(44) | `mode` absent, **None** |
| `@deposito_origine_codice` | `mode='O'`, Bag(23) | `mode` absent, **None** |
| `@deposito_destinazione_codice` | `mode='O'`, Bag(23) | `mode` absent, **None** |
| `@operazione_id` | `mode='O'`, Bag(29) | `mode` absent, **None** |
| `@righe` | `mode='M'`, **Bag(0)** | `mode` absent, **None** |

Note that the main form saves fine: its `@righe` is an *empty Bag*, which the many
loop walks without doing anything. It is the impoverished copy that breaks.

Consequently all five nodes land in `relatedMany` with a `None` value, and the many
loop (crud.py:604-621) raises on the first one. Nothing of value is lost by skipping
them: the FK columns themselves are plain columns of `main_record`.

## Proposed fix

Minimal and local, in the many loop:

```python
for rel_name, rel_recordClusterNode in list(relatedMany.items()):
    rel_recordCluster = rel_recordClusterNode.value
    if not rel_recordCluster:
        continue
```

Two deeper questions, for whoever owns this area:

1. Should `_splitRecordCluster` resolve the relation kind from the model rather than
   trusting the `mode` attribute? That would stop an FK node from ever being treated
   as a many relation, whatever the cluster's provenance.
2. Should the `GroupletForm` store copy preserve relation node attributes — or strip
   relation nodes entirely, given the step form has no UI bound to them?

## Environment

- genropy `release-26.07.17-54-g4aa37301e` (branch `fix/service-implementations-race`)
- Python 3.13.2, PostgreSQL, multidb instance
- macOS 26.0.1, Chrome

## Related finding

Same setup, separate defect. `groupletWizard` mounts its step `GroupletForm` with
`loadOnBuilt=True`, which should emit `this.form.load()` through the grouplet's
`_onRemote` (genro_components.js:1037-1042). On this form-only page it never fires:
the step form stays at `status='noItem'`, and since a form with no record disables
every widget, the whole wizard renders as frozen — the fields grey out as soon as the
user touches one. Calling `load()` explicitly re-enables it; from the step's own
`grouplet_main` it only works when deferred (`genro.callAfter`), which suggests the
step form is not ready at grouplet build time.

This silent-failure mode may belong to the scope of #909.

items.title: fix(gnrjs): drop the subscriptions of content discarded under a frozen node

labels.name: Needs attention
labels.description: The issue is clear and is ready to be managed

items.body:
## Problem

Since a batch ends, the console fills with `unresolved relativepath .?progress` (and `.?maximum`, `.?indeterminate`, `.?places`) from `absDatapath`, once per thermoline attribute, at every data change under `gnr.batch.<id>`. For developers each one is a `debugger` stop.

## Root cause

Not the datachange PRs (#1248, #1258): batch changes travel with `tl_*`/`btc_*` reasons and never touch the `serverChange` branch. The origin is #1152 (path-indexed trigger dispatch, 26 Aug), with #1207 on top.

- `batch_monitor.btc_result` does `resultNode.freeze(); resultNode.clearValue();` (`batch_handler.js:146`).
- `clearValue` detaches the old content with a recursive `clearBackRef()` — that is why the message shows `.?progress` with no `.<code>` segment: the very first `getParentNode()` is already null.
- The `upd` trigger reaches `GnrSrcHandler.nodeTrigger`, which returns at once on a frozen node. `_trigger_upd` never runs, so the incremental `cleanupContentSubscriptions(oldvalue)` introduced by #1152 never runs either: every `^.?progress` subscription of the progressBars stays in the trie under `gnr.batch.<id>.thermo.<code>`.
- `unfreeze()` → `rebuild()` is a same-bag rebuild, which #1207 deliberately leaves alone.
- Before #1152 `refreshSourceIndexAndSubscribers()` ran on every `_trigger_upd`/`_trigger_del` anywhere in the page and swept the subscriptions of nodes no longer in the tree: the leak was reabsorbed at the next rebuild. The incremental cleanup has exactly one hole: content discarded while its node is frozen.

Then `btc_result_doc` writes `gnr.batch.<id>`; the `^gnr.batch` dataController (indexed on the ancestor, visited first) runs `btc_result`, and in the same `publish` loop the detached subtree subscriptions are reached.

## Blast radius

Same freeze-then-discard idiom, out of the 52 `freeze()` sites in gnrjs and resources:

- `timesheet_viewer.js:91` and `:424` — `freeze().clearValue()`
- `grouplet_grid.js:2253` — `tileNode.freeze()` then `popNode` in `_destroyChrome`/`_destroyBody`: the `del` event is skipped the same way

The `setValue(x, false)` sites on source nodes (menu, `setSource`, `_`, closable wrapper, grid editor) are pre-build: nothing is subscribed yet. The dialogs use `clearValue().freeze()`, the right order.

## Change

`nodeTrigger` keeps deferring the DOM rebuild while the node is frozen, but cleans up what was discarded right away: the node's own subtree on `del`, the replaced bag on `upd`. A same-bag rebuild (`oldvalue === node._value`) is still untouched, as in #1207. The `_isBuilding` early return is unchanged.

No change to `batch_handler.js`: the fix lands in the shared handler, where the hole is.

## Verification

- New `gnrjs/tests/trigger_index_frozen_discard.test.js` (`node:test` + `vm`, same harness as `external_change.test.js`, loading `genro_src.js` too). It builds the batch monitor shape without a DOM and covers: the subscription is indexed under the absolute path; content cleared under freeze leaves the index; a node popped under a frozen ancestor leaves the index; a same-bag rebuild under freeze keeps the subscriptions; a frozen node with no discarded content is left alone. The two discard cases are **red before the change, green after** (verified by stashing the fix).
- `node --test gnrjs/tests/` — 36 passed.
- `node --check gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_src.js` clean.
- Not verified in a browser: the effect on the running batch monitor is deduced from the code paths above.

## Residual risk

A data node (`dataController`, `_alreadyStripped`) popped and reinserted under a frozen ancestor would lose its subscription. None of the freeze sites found moves nodes; they discard and recreate. Not verified exhaustively.

## Related

#1300 proposes reporting lost-node subscriptions in `GnrTriggerIndex.publish` with a dedicated error, so that any future leak points at its discard path instead of at `absDatapath`.

items.body:
## Summary

Introduce **`groupletGrid`**, a genropy widget that renders a Bag as N tiles where each tile is the same reusable "grouplet" template (a mini-form). One RPC for the row template at boot, then **zero RPC** for every add / remove / edit / save — everything flows through Bag triggers.

It targets use cases that don't fit a flat `gnr.Grid`: invoice line editors, kanban boards, framed card galleries, spreadsheet-style data entry (`struct=` mode), multi-pane tab editors, and recursive master-detail forms.

## What's in

- **Python helper** `gr_groupletGrid(...)` (`resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.py`) — emits a CSS-grid container with autoslots (top/bottom/left/right), a sibling `BagStore` for change/lock/delete integration, and a `_onBuilt` dataController that boots the JS controller.

- **JS controller** (`resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet_grid.js`) — five `gnr.*` classes:
  - `GroupletGridStructAdapter` — maps a Grid-style `struct` to a spreadsheet-like tile.
  - `GroupletGridDnD` — DOM-pure HTML5 drag-and-drop dispatcher shared by tile and chip paths.
  - `GroupletGridController` — lifecycle, action bus, layout switching, template loading (with `resourceField=` multi-template mode), `GridChangeManager` bridge for formulas / totalizers.
  - `GroupletGridTile` — per-pkey view with chrome (×, kebab, drag handle ⠿) and body grafted from a deep-copied template.
  - `GroupletDataStore` — thin view over the sibling `BagStore`; forwards getData / addRow / removeRow / moveRow / updateRow / deleteRowAsk / hasChanges / hasErrors / setLocked.

- **CSS** (`resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/grouplet.css`) — theme tokens, layout primitives for cards / tabs / vtabs / struct modes, DnD state classes aligned with framework conventions (`draggedItem`, `canBeDropped`, `cannotBeDropped`, `body.drag_started`).

## Demo gallery

All demos live under `projects/gnrcore/packages/test/webpages/gnrwdg/test_grouplet_grid/`:

| Page | Scenario |
|---|---|
| `01_gallery.py::test_01_invoice_baseline` | invoice baseline (cards single-grid) |
| `test_02_todolist_handler` | todolist via handler callable |
| `test_03_invoice_responsive` | responsive cols + min_width |
| `test_04_kanban_dnd` | kanban with cross-grid DnD (`dragCode='kanban'`) |
| `test_05_team_tabs` | team tabs — tabs/vtabs/cards layout switch with nested contacts |
| `test_06_struct_shopping_list` | struct shopping list — totalize + formula |
| `test_07_myticket_resourcefield` | resourceField multi-template (myticket with 9 grouplets) |
| `02_grid_db.py` | DB-backed via `thFormHandler` + nested groupletGrid over `glbl.provincia` |
| `03_budget_editor.py` | realistic 3-level nested editor (chapters → accounts → details, all struct-mode) |
| `04_perf_50.py` | 50 realistic instances on a single page — bootstrap-time probe for the always-on sibling BagStore |

The test package contains a small **TableHandler overlay** at `projects/gnrcore/packages/test/resources/tables/_packages/glbl/regione/th_regione.py` that augments the base `th_regione.py` from `gnr_it`. Reason: the `02_grid_db.py` demo needs a regione + province editing UI scoped to the test package, without modifying the upstream `gnr_it` handler.

## Design decisions worth flagging

1. **Sibling `BagStore` is mandatory** (default `storeType='ValuesBagRows'`). The container exposes `attr.store=<bagStore nodeId>`; the dataStore looks it up via `genro.nodeById`. The trade-off is one extra sourceNode + a thin wrapper object per grid (no data duplication). Mandatory because every meaningful integration — `GridChangeManager`, `deleteAsk`, future phantomForm and filter-aware totals — hangs off the store. Reverting later would be a breaking change. The `04_perf_50.py` probe measures the actual overhead at scale.

2. **Framework nodeId namespacing through a static whitelist**. `_namespaceFrameworkNodeIds` rewrites `grpgrid_*` string values for a closed set of attribute keys (`nodeId`, `store`, `storeCode`, `dragCode`) in cloned templates. Required so cross-references inside cloned templates stay consistent per row. Side effect: `dragCode=None` (default-isolated) is now genuinely per-instance; cross-grid sharing requires an explicit string `dragCode` — `test_04` shows this convention.

3. **DOM-pure DnD on both tile and chip**. No framework `dropTarget`/`onDrag_*` kwargs anywhere. Same pattern on both, decoupled from `getInheritedAttributes` / pointer-events cascades that historically broke nested grids.

4. **Move dispatch splices `bag._nodes` in place** (no `popNode + setItem(_position)`). Nested widgets anchored at the moved row's datapath would otherwise see `unresolved relativepath`. Documented inline.

5. **Construct-time controller work deferred to `genro.src.onBuiltCall`**. Same pattern as gnr.Grid (`genro_grid.js:704`): cloned templates finish building their inner `BagStore` after the controller's own `_onBuilt` fires.

## What's not in (future PRs)

- **Filter + sort** applied visually (`display:none` on filtered-out tiles + `style.order` per visible tile) on top of the store's `_filtered` array, so `GridChangeManager` totals aggregate the visible rows for free. The four `setFilter/clearFilter/setSort/clearSort` no-op stubs on `GroupletDataStore` are placeholders for this work.
- **`AttributesBagRows` adapter** so `storeType='Selection'` or `'RpcBase'` work uniformly (DB-backed grids without manual materialisation).
- **phantomForm integration** for per-tile edit lifecycle and validation gates.

These are deliberate scope cuts — the widget is already useful for in-memory editors and the future work hangs off the foundations introduced here.

## Test plan

- [x] Manual browser smoke test: `test_01`, `test_04` (kanban cross-grid), `test_05` (tabs + nested), `test_06` (struct), `02_grid_db`, `03_budget_editor`
- [x] Cross-browser manual verification — gallery exercised on Chrome, Safari and Firefox; all OK
- [x] `04_perf_50.py` — 50 realistic instances render and bootstrap correctly; the always-on sibling `BagStore` does not surface measurable overhead at this scale
- [x] `pytest` — 1553 passed, 260 skipped, 0 new failures (pre-existing unrelated skips)
- [x] `flake8` on `resources/common/gnrcomponents/grouplet/` and changed Python files — clean
- [x] `node -c grouplet_grid.js` — clean

## Review feedback addressed (commit `665757574`)

- **Demo reorg**: new dedicated folder `test_grouplet_grid/` collecting gallery + db demo + budget editor + perf probe (was spread across `test_grouplets/` and `budget_editor/`). Gallery trimmed from 12 to 7 tests; orphan resources (`shopping_row.py`, `excel_row.py`) removed.
- **Refactor**: `gr_groupletGrid` `_onBuilt` bootstrap extracted to `_gr_groupletGrid_emitController` (216 → 167 lines). `_namespaceFrameworkNodeIds` uses a static whitelist instead of scanning every attribute. `_syncStructChromeToColumns` split into `_frameStructChromeToFirstRow` + `_placeStructColumnCells`.
- **Stubs**: Phase 2 `setFilter`/`clearFilter`/`setSort`/`clearSort` are now silent no-ops (no more `console.warn` for every caller in production).
- **Docs**: design content moved to Sourcerer KB skills under `GenroPy/User Interface/Components & Resources/Grouplets/GroupletGrid`; `docs/groupletgrid_architecture.md` and `docs/groupletgrid_store_integration.html` removed from the repo.

items.title: perf(gnrjs): path-indexed trigger dispatch, per-handler caches and bag hot paths

labels.name: Needs attention
labels.description: The issue is clear and is ready to be managed

items.body:
## What

Profiling-driven optimization of the client engine (gnrjs) for very large pages, plus the profiling infrastructure used to find the real bottlenecks and a document with the findings.

Measured on the new `test/perf/test_heavy_build` page (~8.200 source nodes, ~1.400 dojo widgets), median of 6 runs:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `startUp` build | 1609 ms | 514 ms (3.1x) |
| 600 `setData` on bound fields | 384 ms | 30 ms (13x) |

## How

- **`gnr.GnrTriggerIndex`** (genro_src.js): dynamic `^attr` subscriptions with a stable absolute datapath are indexed in a trie by path segments; an event reaches only the nodes on its path, its ancestors or its subtree instead of every subscription on the page (2.55M `trigger_data` calls for 600 setData before). Subscriptions with pointer/symbolic datapaths stay in a floating set checked on every event as before; `trigger_data` keeps its full semantic check, so routing false positives are harmless. The `_trigger_data` dojo topic is still published for the direct subscribers (grid cellpars, tree).
- **Incremental subscriber cleanup**: `_trigger_del`/`_trigger_upd` clean only the removed subtree instead of rebuilding index and subscriptions with a full source-tree walk per trigger.
- **`getFormHandler` negative caching**: nodes outside any form stop at their parent instead of walking to the root per node.
- **Widget factory cache** keyed by the resolved dojo tag (handlers like menuline switch `_dojotag` per instance) and **per-handler mixin plan** replacing the per-widget scan of every handler property. Largest single build win; also removes most build-time GC noise (variance ±20% → ±3%).
- **Bag hot paths**: `htraverse` fast path for single plain labels, `walk` static mode without `getValue`, `fromXmlDoc` single conversion (plain strings untouched), `_pop` array-replacement behavior documented (callers iterate `_nodes` while popping).
- **FramePane** uniqueness assert on the nodeId index instead of a full-tree `nodeById` probe.

Details, methodology and remaining margins in `docs/architecture/client_performance.md`. Remaining margins tracked in #1151.

## Verification

- Real-browser regression pass: `plainTableHandler` (data, searchbox filter, autoSelect), `test_flex_minwidth` (bagGrid, columnsets), sandbox app th pages (Clienti/Fatture) with menus/dialogs, heavy page (bound fields receive values, validations, 8 grids with 200 rows, 3000 dynamic divs, data storm, tab rebuild) - no new console errors.
- Two approaches were tried and reverted after breaking tablehandler pages in the browser (batch nodeId pre-index, in-place `_pop` splice); both are documented in the doc so they are not retried blindly.
- Full python test suite green (pre-commit hook), flake8 clean on the new test page.

Fixes #1146

items.title: fix(groupletGrid): isolate sibling bagStore on workspace controller path
items.body:
## Summary

- The sibling `bagStore` emitted by `groupletGrid` inherited the container's `datapath`. CollectionStore base methods write control flags via `storeNode.setRelativeData('.locked', ...)` / `.disabledButton` (`setLocked`), so those flags landed **sibling to the rows Bag** — inside the host form's data area — and marked the form dirty on every lock/unlock toggle.
- In **workspace mode** (the default, when no explicit `structpath` is passed) the bagStore's `storeNode` is now parked under `#WORKSPACE.store`, isolated per-instance like the struct already is. The rows `storepath` is anchored to the container via `#<nodeId>` so the rows Bag resolves to the same node regardless of where `storeNode` lives.
- When the caller pinned `structpath` explicitly (no workspace mode), behaviour is unchanged — the caller has chosen where the grouplet's state lives and is responsible for placing `datapath` out of the edit area if needed.

## Mechanism

- `#WORKSPACE` and `#<nodeId>` are existing anchors handled by `symbolicDatapath` (`gnrjs/gnr_d20/js/gnrdomsource.js`). `BagRows` resolves `storepath` via `storeNode.absDatapath(...)` which honours both forms — no JS changes needed.
- `setLocked` keeps writing `.locked` / `.disabledButton` relative to `storeNode`, but `storeNode.datapath` now points to `gnr.workspace.<nodeId>.store` instead of the container's data area.
- `grouplet_grid.js` controller is unaffected: it looks up the sibling store via `genro.nodeById(<storeCode>).store` (nodeId-based, not datapath-based) and reads `storebag().getParentNode()` on the data Bag (not on the DOM source node).
- d11/d20 are both covered automatically by the Python-side change; `genro_components.js` is untouched in both bundles.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a form hosting a `groupletGrid` (default args, no explicit `structpath`). Verify the record is clean.
- [ ] Toggle lock/unlock on the grid → form must stay clean (today it goes dirty).
- [ ] Insert / update / delete / move rows → data must roundtrip to the same path as before (check via `genro.getData(<abs_storepath>)`).
- [ ] Save the form after a lock toggle → server must not receive any `.locked` / `.disabledButton` field.
- [ ] Test against a page with explicit `structpath` (non-workspace branch) → behaviour identical to current.
- [ ] Spot-check on both d11 and d20 bundles.

## Summary Major enhancements to the grouplet system, introducing new layout modes, navigation components, and developer-friendly auto-discovery features. ### New Components - **`groupletPanel`** — Tree-based or multibutton navigation for browsing grouplet menus with content area - **`groupletWizard`** — Step-by-step form flow with a visual stepper bar, validation gating, and memory store integration - **Topic-as-resource grid** — When a topic folder is passed as resource, all child grouplets render in a CSS grid layout ### New Features - **Template auto-discovery** — `groupletChunk` reads `template` and `template_virtual_columns` from the resource `__info__.py`, removing the need for explicit parameters - **Collapsible grid cells** — Topic grid cells can be toggled open/closed via header click (`grid_collapsible=True|'closed'`) - **Non-table grouplets** — App-level grouplet resources that don't require a table binding - **Nested topics** — Multi-level resource paths (e.g. `territorio/altimetria`) - **GroupletForm `loadOnBuilt`/`startKey`** — Immediate form loading on widget build - **Formstore `load_rpc`/`save_rpc`** — Generic RPC methods on the Base formstore class - **Terminology refactor** — Renamed `group` → `topic` throughout the grouplet API ### New Assets - `grouplet.css` — Styles for topic grids, wizard stepper, collapsible cells, tree panel - `grouplet.js` — Client logic for wizard navigation, cell toggle, panel selection --- ## Documentation & Usage Examples ### Grouplet Resource Structure Grouplets are organized as Python resource files under `resources/tables//grouplets/` or `resources/grouplets/` (for non-table grouplets). Each file defines an `info` dict and a `Grouplet` class: ```python # resources/tables/myticket/grouplets/technical/system.py from gnr.web.gnrbaseclasses import BaseComponent info = dict( caption='System Info', code='system', priority=1 ) class Grouplet(BaseComponent): def grouplet_main(self, pane, **kwargs): fb = pane.formlet(cols=2, border_spacing='3px', table='test.myticket') fb.field('operating_system', lbl='OS') fb.field('software_version', lbl='Version') fb.field('browser', lbl='Browser') ``` ### Topics (Folders of Grouplets) A **topic** is a folder containing multiple related grouplets and an `__info__.py`: ``` grouplets/ ├── technical/ │ ├── __info__.py # topic metadata + optional template │ ├── system.py │ ├── error.py │ └── reproduction.py ├── commercial/ │ ├── __info__.py │ ├── company.py │ ├── contract.py │ └── offer.py ``` The `__info__.py` defines topic-level metadata and an optional template for `groupletChunk` previews: ```python # __info__.py info = dict( caption='Technical Details', priority=1, template='
${OS: $operating_system}' '${Error: $error_code — $error_message}
' ) ``` ### Topic-as-Resource Grid Pass a topic folder name as the `resource` parameter. All child grouplets render in a CSS grid: ```python # Single column (default) pane.grouplet(resource='technical', table='test.myticket', value='^.extra_data') # Two-column grid pane.grouplet(resource='technical', table='test.myticket', value='^.extra_data', remote_grid_columns=2) # Collapsible cells, start closed pane.grouplet(resource='technical', table='test.myticket', value='^.extra_data', remote_grid_collapsible='closed') ``` ### groupletChunk with Auto-Discovery The template is automatically read from the topic's `__info__.py`: ```python # No need to specify template= or virtual_columns= pane.groupletChunk(value='^.extra_data', name='technical_data', resource='technical', table='test.myticket', title='Technical') ``` ### groupletPanel Tree-based navigation with a content area: ```python pane.groupletPanel(table='test.myticket', value='^.extra_data', height='400px') ``` With topic filter and multibutton mode (ideal for mobile): ```python pane.groupletPanel(table='test.myticket', topic='technical', value='^.extra_data') ``` ### groupletWizard Step-by-step form filling: ```python pane.groupletWizard(table='test.booking', topic='booking', value='^.extra_data', completeLabel='Confirm Booking', height='400px') ``` ### Non-Table Grouplets Grouplets can live under `resources/grouplets/` without table binding: ```python pane.groupletPanel(topic='app', value='^.app_settings') ``` --- ## Test Plan - [x] flake8 passes with zero errors on all modified files - [x] Full test suite passes (1305 passed, 147 skipped) - [x] Manual testing of topic grid layouts (1-col, 2-col, collapsible) - [x] Manual testing of groupletWizard step navigation - [x] Manual testing of groupletPanel tree and multibutton modes - [x] Manual testing of groupletChunk template auto-discovery - [x] Manual testing of non-table grouplets

items.title: fix(#686): restore custom rpcmethod in document store load
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #686 — `IsADirectoryError` when opening the Localization Editor.

## Root cause

The grouplets refactoring (PR #560, commit `d98a4cf56f`) rewrote `load_document` in `genro_frm.js` and hardcoded `'getSiteDocument'` as the RPC method:

```javascript
// NEW (broken) — ignores custom handler
kw.rpcmethod = kw.rpcmethod || 'getSiteDocument';
```

The **original** code respected the custom `rpcmethod` set via `form.store.handler('load', rpcmethod=...)`:

```javascript
// OLD (working) — custom handler first, default as fallback
this.handlers.load.rpcmethod = loader.rpcmethod || 'getSiteDocument';
```

The Localization Editor uses `store='document'` with a custom handler (`loadLocalizationFile`) that knows how to handle directory paths (it does `os.path.join(path, 'localization.xml')`). After the regression, `getSiteDocument` was called instead, which tried to `open()` a directory path — crash.

## Fix

Restore the original priority chain in `load_document`:

```javascript
kw.rpcmethod = kw.rpcmethod || this.handlers.load.rpcmethod || 'getSiteDocument';
```

Also reverts the symptomatic `snode.isdir` guard on `getSiteDocument` (commit `aed62de316`) which masked the real cause without fixing it.

## Files changed

- `gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_frm.js` — restore handler rpcmethod priority
- `gnrjs/gnr_d20/js/genro_frm.js` — same fix for dojo_20
- `gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwebpage.py` — revert isdir workaround

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a Genropy app with localization (e.g. any app with `adm` package)
- [ ] Navigate to **System → Localization Editor**
- [ ] Select the **core** block — should load without error
- [ ] Select package blocks — should also load correctly
- [ ] Verify that other `store='document'` forms still work (e.g. doc_handler)

items.body:
## Summary

- Fix regression in `quickDialog` `close_action` that throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'popNode')` when closing dialogs opened from button/slotbutton nodes
- Root cause: the `_resolveDialogRoot` refactoring moved the rootNode walk-up logic into a separate method, but the caller's `rootNode` parameter was no longer reassigned — the `close_action` closure captured the original (unwalkable) node instead of the resolved parent
- `_resolveDialogRoot` now returns the resolved root node; both callers (`quickDialog` and `_groupletForm`) reassign `rootNode` and extract the child node themselves

## Details

When `quickDialog` is called with a `rootNode` that is a `button`, `slotbutton`, or similar skipTag node, `_resolveDialogRoot` walks up the tree to find a suitable parent and creates the dialog div there. Before the refactoring, this walk happened inline in `quickDialog`, so the local `rootNode` variable (captured by the `close_action` closure) pointed to the correct parent. After the extraction into `_resolveDialogRoot`, the walk only modified a local parameter inside that method — the caller's `rootNode` remained unchanged, pointing to the original button node whose `getValue()` returns `null`.

## Test plan

- [x] Open a page that triggers `quickDialog` from a button/slotbutton node
- [x] Open and close the dialog — no `popNode` TypeError
- [x] Verify grouplet dialogs (`_groupletForm` path) still open and close correctly
